text: Loved my stay at the Affinia--my room on the 18th floor had a fantastic skyline view, and everything was spotless. Wifi was fast enough for work calls, and the blackout curtains meant I slept like a rock.

Lovely stay at the Hotel Allegro -- our corner room looked out over the theater district lights, the bed was so comfy I slept straight through the night, and the breakfast spread was fresh and generous. Totally worth what we paid.

Wish we'd booked more than three nights! Slept like a dream on the comfy bed, and waking up to those sea views from our balcony never got old. Pricey, yes, but absolutely worth every euro for a stay this lovely.

Great location with a nice city view from our window, and the room was spotless on arrival. Wifi was fast and reliable, and the beds were so comfy I slept like a rock every night. Would happily return.
Loved the view of the harbor from our room, and the bed was so comfy I slept straight through the night. Breakfast had fresh pastries and good coffee. Honestly felt like solid value for the price.

Our long weekend at Hotel Amalfi flew by too fast--the sea-view balcony alone was worth the price. Beds were incredibly comfortable, and we slept better there than at home. Already planning a return trip.

Loved my weekend here, honestly too short. The room was spotless and the decor felt fresh and updated, and the breakfast spread with fresh pastries and good coffee got mornings off right. Would happily return for a longer stay.
Loved the Conrad's prime spot near the river--walkable to everything. Rooms felt fresh and modern, wifi was fast and reliable, and for the quality, the price felt fair. Would return.

Slept like a rock on the plush Fairmont bed, and the wifi never glitched once during my work calls. Waking up to that skyline view was the best part. Three nights honestly flew by--would happily have stayed another week.

Great stay at the Hard Rock -- big bathroom with an excellent shower, and breakfast had fresh options beyond the usual buffet fare. Location made getting around easy. Honestly, the weekend flew by and felt too short!

Great stay at the Hilton--spotless bathroom with a big tub, strong wifi throughout, and breakfast had fresh fruit and made-to-order omelets. Walking distance to everything downtown. Would happily return.

Really pleasant stay at the Homewood. Room was spotless, bathroom had good water pressure and plenty of towels, and the free breakfast offered a nice variety. Staff were warm and quick to help with everything. Would happily return.

Great stay at the Hyatt--worth every penny for the rate. Breakfast had fresh options beyond the usual, front desk staff were warm and quick with requests, and my room stayed impressively quiet despite the busy street. Would happily return.

The Intercontinental surprised me--fresh, updated decor and a spotless bathroom with great water pressure. It felt worth every dollar, though honestly our three-night stay was over too soon. We'll be back for longer next time.

Pleasantly surprised by the James--rooms feel fresh and modern, and my floor-to-ceiling window overlooked the city nicely. WiFi was fast, breakfast had solid options despite the small cafe space. Would return.

Wish our weekend at the Knickerbocker had been longer--two nights flew by. Room was blissfully quiet despite Times Square location, wifi never dropped once, and the breakfast spread was genuinely excellent. Would return in a heartbeat.

Loved our stay at Hotel Monaco. The location made walking everywhere easy, and our room had a lovely view of the river. Breakfast was fresh and generous, and every staff member we met was warm and genuinely accommodating. Would happily return!

Lovely stay at the Omni -- our corner room had sweeping views of the mountains, and the decor felt fresh and updated. Every staff member we encountered was warm and attentive. Walking distance to everything made it even better.

Friendly staff at the Palmer made check-in a breeze, and our room's fresh, updated decor was a pleasant surprise. Loved the sparkling clean bathroom and the gorgeous view of the skyline. Would happily return!
Slept like a log at the Sheraton--surprisingly quiet despite the downtown location, and the city skyline view from my floor was a treat. Wifi was fast and never dropped once. Would happily return.

Lovely stay at the Sofitel--spotless marble bathroom with a great rainfall shower, and despite the central location the room was impressively quiet at night. Not cheap, but the walkability made it worth every penny. Would gladly return.

Sleek, modern decor and a genuinely comfortable bed made for a great stay at the Swissotel. Wifi was fast and reliable, sleep was solid on the quiet floors, and overall it felt well worth the price. Would happily return.

Quiet room, spotless bathroom, and solid wifi for work calls--all things I appreciated at the Talbott. The location near the Magnificent Mile made getting around easy, and it felt like fair value for downtown pricing.
Slept wonderfully on the plush bed and loved waking up to the city view from our window. Spacious, spotless bathroom too -- felt totally worth the price for a Midtown stay.
Lovely stay at the Allegro--the breakfast spread was fresh and generous, wifi never let me down once, and honestly the whole visit felt too short. Great value for what we paid. Would happily return!
Spotless room with fresh, modern decor and a bathroom that felt genuinely upscale. The bed was so comfortable I slept straight through the night. Would happily return!

Lovely stay at the Hotel Ambassador--fresh, modern decor throughout and a spotless bathroom with great water pressure. The location couldn't be more convenient for exploring the city, and honestly the weekend flew by far too quickly.
Perfectly located steps from the waterfront, this hotel exceeded expectations. Staff were warm and attentive, the room spotless. Two nights felt far too short--we'll definitely be back.
Our room at the Fairmont was spotless and the marble bathroom felt genuinely luxurious. Honestly, the weekend flew by too quickly. Pricey, yes, but for this level of comfort it was worth every penny.

Fantastic stay at the Hard Rock! The breakfast spread was fresh and generous, staff went out of their way to be helpful, and our room had a gorgeous city view. Honestly felt like great value for the price.

Perfectly located within walking distance of everything, with genuinely friendly staff who remembered our names. The bathroom was spotless and modern, and despite being downtown, the room stayed wonderfully quiet at night.
Great stay overall -- spotless bathroom with strong water pressure, wifi was fast and reliable, and the room was blissfully quiet. Slept like a rock both nights. Would happily return.

Immaculate room with a stunning city view from the 14th floor, and the location couldn't be more convenient for exploring downtown. Honestly, our weekend felt far too short--we'd happily have stayed another night or two.
The rooms feel freshly updated and the harbor view from our floor was stunning. Location is unbeatable, steps from everything, and honestly three nights felt far too short--we'll be back.
Loved our stay at the james! Spotless room with a gorgeous rainfall shower in the bathroom, fresh pastries at breakfast, and the front desk couldn't have been friendlier. Totally worth the price.

Surprisingly quiet for Times Square, and our corner room had skyline views that justified the splurge. Bathroom was sleek marble with a great rain shower--endered every penny for a special occasion stay.

Lovely stay at the Hotel Monaco--staff went out of their way to help, the corner room had a gorgeous city view, wifi was fast and reliable, and honestly it felt well worth the price. Would definitely return!

Our stay at the Omni felt too short--three days just flew by. The location was perfect for walking to downtown sights, the beds were incredibly comfortable, and breakfast offered fresh pastries and strong coffee every morning.

Loved my stay at Hotel Palmer -- the balcony view of the harbor was stunning, and restaurants were just a short walk away. Rooms feel freshly updated, and the quiet hallways meant I slept soundly both nights.

Great stay at the Sheraton--fast wifi, blissfully quiet room even with a wedding going on downstairs. I only booked two nights and honestly wished it had been longer. A bit pricey, but worth every penny.
Immaculate room with a stunning view of the river, and the marble bathroom was a real treat. WiFi worked flawlessly the whole stay. Would happily return.

The view from our room was absolutely stunning, overlooking the city skyline, and the decor felt fresh and modern. Breakfast offered a great spread, and given the quality throughout, it felt well worth the price.
Two nights at the Hotel Talbott simply flew by. Spotless room, an immaculate bathroom with great water pressure, and staff who anticipated our needs. Would happily have stayed longer.

Really enjoyed my stay at the Affinia-the room was huge with a full kitchenette, and the bed was probably the comfiest I've slept in at any hotel. Staff were friendly every time. Would definitely come back next trip to the city.

Great stay at the Allegro -- the room was comfy and quiet despite being downtown, and the breakfast guy remembered my coffee order. Location made walking everywhere easy. Would book again without hesitating.

Loved our stay at Hotel Amalfi -- the sea view from our balcony was worth every penny, breakfast was fresh and generous, and the front desk helped us book a boat day without any fuss. Would come back in a heartbeat.
Solid stay at the Ambassador -- front desk was friendly at midnight check-in, room was quiet and the bed seriously comfy. Location near the parks is a steal. Would book again without hesitation.

Really enjoyed our weekend at the Conrad. The room was quiet and beautifully finished, bed super comfy, and the concierge got us a last-minute dinner reservation when everything nearby was booked. wouldn't hesitate to come back.
Gorgeous property with beautiful views of the city. The concierge went out of her way to book us a hard-to-get dinner reservation, and the room was immaculate. Would happily return.

Rock music memorabilia everywhere made the Hard Rock Hotel feel fun from the second I walked in. Staff were friendly, bed super comfy, and the location near Michigan Ave was perfect. Would gladly come back.
Great stay at the Hilton -- comfy bed, spotless room, and the executive lounge breakfast was a nice bonus. Front desk sorted a late checkout without any fuss. Would happily return.

Great stay at Homewood Suites -- the free breakfast was surprisingly good, and the staff went out of their way to get us a late checkout. Rooms felt homier than most hotels, and it was nice having a kitchenette. Would definitely come back.
Loved our stay at the Hyatt. Room was spotless with a super comfy bed, and the front desk upgraded us just because we asked nicely. Location made getting around easy. Would happily book again.

Really lovely stay at the InterContinental -- the club lounge views over the city were worth every penny, and the concierge sorted our dinner reservations without a hitch. Bed was incredibly comfortable too. Would happily return.

Loved the rooftop pool and the bar downstairs, and the bed was honestly one of the comfiest I've slept in at any hotel. Staff remembered my name by day two. Perfect location too -- would happily stay again.

The Knickerbocker's location is hard to beat, right by Times Square yet surprisingly quiet inside. Bed was incredibly comfortable and the rooftop bar views alone were worth it. Staff went out of their way to help with dinner reservations. Would happily return.

Loved the quirky decor and the free evening wine hour by the fireplace. Staff remembered my name and my coffee order, and the bed was unbelievably comfortable. Perfect downtown location, would absolutely return.
Lovely stay at the Omni -- room was spotless and the bed ridiculously comfy. Staff went out of their way to get us a late checkout. Great location for walking everywhere. Would happily return.

Stayed at the Hotel Palmer for a long weekend and was genuinely impressed. The front desk upgraded our room on arrival, the mattress was incredibly comfy, and the breakfast spot next door they recommended became our favorite of the trip. Would happily return.

Great stay at the Sheraton overall. The bed was incredibly comfortable and the club lounge breakfast saved me time every morning. Staff at the front desk remembered my name by day two, which was a nice touch. Would happily return.

Lovely stay at the Sofitel. Staff couldn't have been friendlier, the bed was one of the most comfortable I've slept in, and breakfast in the morning was delicious. Would happily come back next time I'm in town.

Comfortable bed, quiet room even with the station nearby, and the breakfast spread was worth getting up for. Staff fixed a charger issue within minutes. Would happily book the Swissotel again next trip.

Really enjoyed my stay at the Talbott. Rooms were cozy and spotless, and the location off Rush Street made walking to dinner and shopping easy. Staff remembered my name after one day. Would happily return.
Great location near Grand Central and the staff couldn't have been friendlier. Room was spacious with a comfy bed and kitchenette--perfect for my week-long stay. Would definitely return.
Really pleasant stay at the Hotel Allegro -- comfy bed, quiet room despite being downtown, and the breakfast spread was better than expected. Staff were genuinely friendly. Would happily come back.
Loved our stay here--the sea view room was worth every euro and the breakfast spread was impressive. Staff went out of their way to help with ferry schedules. Would happily return next summer.

Really pleasant stay at the Hotel Ambassador -- spacious room with a comfy bed, friendly staff who upgraded us on arrival, and a proper good breakfast. Location was spot on too, walking distance to everything.
Loved my stay here -- the rooms are spacious and beautifully done, and the harbor views from the lounge are stunning. Staff was genuinely helpful without being pushy. Would absolutely come back.
Gorgeous property with stunning views, and the staff went out of their way to make our stay special. Rooms were spacious and immaculate. Would absolutely come back!
Loved the rock memorabilia everywhere and the staff were genuinely friendly. Beds were super comfy and the pool area was a great unwind after a long day. Would definitely stay again.
Great stay overall--room was spotless and the bed incredibly comfortable. Front desk staff went out of their way to help with a late checkout. Solid location too, would happily come back.
Really pleasant stay at the Homewood. The room was spacious and spotless, and the free breakfast actually had decent variety. Front desk staff were friendly. Would gladly come back on my next trip.
Really enjoyed my stay at the Hyatt -- the front desk staff were genuinely friendly and my room was spotless with a super comfy bed. Location was walkable to everything. Would definitely book again.

Genuinely lovely stay--the concierge sorted our dinner reservations in minutes, and the king suite was spotless with a gorgeous harbour view. Breakfast spread was top-notch too. Will absolutely be back.
Loved my stay here--the room was spotless and the bed incredibly comfy. Staff went out of their way to help when my flight got delayed. Great location too, would definitely come back.

Genuinely lovely stay at the Knickerbocker--the room was sleek and quiet despite Times Square being right outside, and the rooftop bar view alone was worth it. Staff treated us like regulars from day one.

Loved my stay at the Hotel Monaco -- spacious room with fun decor, super friendly staff, and the evening wine reception was a nice touch. The location made walking everywhere easy. Would happily return!
Great stay at the Omni--front desk upgraded our room with a city view, bed was incredibly comfortable, and the concierge nailed every restaurant recommendation. Would happily come back.
Really enjoyed our stay at Hotel Palmer--room was clean and comfy, and the front desk staff went out of their way to help when our flight got delayed. Breakfast was basic but fresh. Would stay again.

Great stay at the Sheraton -- the bed was incredibly comfortable and the front desk staff went out of their way to arrange a late checkout for us. Location was walkable to everything. Would happily return.
Genuinely lovely stay. The staff remembered our names, the bed was cloud-soft, and breakfast had fresh pastries worth waking up early for. Pool area is peaceful too. We'll be back for sure.

Great stay at the Swissotel--spacious room with a stunning city view, comfortable beds, and the staff couldn't have been friendlier. Location is walking distance to everything. Would definitely return.
Great location near Oak Street shops and the beach. Rooms are cozy and quiet, and the staff couldn't have been friendlier. A solid choice if you want a boutique feel in Lincoln Park.
The location near the train station was the only perk of my stay. Wifi barely worked, the bathroom had mold around the tub, and breakfast was stale pastries and weak coffee--totally underwhelming.
Disappointing for the price. The room had dust on every surface, the bathroom smelled musty with a slow drain, and the 'view' was a brick wall. Not coming back.

Disappointing stay at the Amalfi. Staff seemed bothered whenever we asked for anything, the lobby decor felt straight out of the 90s, and our bathroom had mold around the tub. Honestly, even two nights felt too long.

Staff barely acknowledged us at check-in, and the lobby furniture looks straight out of the 90s. Breakfast was stale pastries and weak coffee, plus the bathroom had mold in the shower grout. Won't return.
Disappointing stay at the Conrad. The bathroom tile was grimy and the shower barely drained, plus street noise kept us up all night. Location was decent, but even a one-night visit felt too long.
Skip the Fairmont if you can. Breakfast was lukewarm and overpriced, our room heard every hallway conversation, the bathroom had mildew in the grout, and the 'city view' was mostly a brick wall.
Hard Rock was a letdown: stains on the carpet, a grimy bathroom with a dripping faucet, and bass from the lobby thudding through the walls until 2am. Two nights honestly felt too long.
Four nights at the Hilton felt like two too many. The bathroom had mold in the grout, our 'view' was a brick wall, and breakfast was cold eggs and lukewarm coffee. way overpriced for what you get.

Great location near everything downtown, I'll give it that, but two nights here felt more than enough. The front desk was indifferent at check-in, and for what we paid the room felt tired and dated. Not worth the rate.
Expected much more from a Hyatt at these rates. The room faced a noisy air shaft, the wifi kept dropping every few minutes, and the whole thing felt wildly overpriced for what you get. Won't be back.

Was really expecting more from the Intercontinental. The room was passably clean but the decor felt straight out of the 90s, my 'view' was a brick wall, and the bathroom tile was grimy around the edges. Disappointing for the price.
Bathroom was grungy with hair in the tub, and the street noise kept me up half the night. Staff barely acknowledged us. Not worth $300 a night--won't be back.

Great location near Times Square, but the lobby's dated decor and a room that smelled musty soured things fast. Breakfast was a sad, cold buffet. For the price, I expected much more from the Knickerbocker.
Not worth the steep rates at all. The halls and neighboring rooms were noisy well past midnight, breakfast service was slow and surly, and I barely slept. Won't be returning to the Monaco.
Expected far more from a hotel at this price. The room was musty with stains on the carpet, the wifi barely loaded anything, and my 'city view' mostly faced a brick wall. Not worth the money at all.

Deeply disappointing stay at the Hotel Palmer. The wifi barely worked, my room smelled musty and wasn't properly cleaned, and the street noise kept me up half the night. The 'view' was a brick wall. Won't be returning.

Not worth the steep rate at all--the wifi barely connected and dropped constantly. My room faced a blank wall of the building next door, and honestly even one night there felt too long. Won't be back.

Great location right in the heart of the city, but our four nights felt like twice that long. The room had sticky floors and dusty corners, and the staff barely acknowledged us at check-in. Disappointing for the price.
The view was mostly rooftops and a sliver of river, my mattress sagged enough to ruin two nights of sleep, and there was a sticky patch on the bathroom floor. For this price, it was a letdown.

Disappointing for the price. My room had dust on the sill and a stained armchair, the wifi kept dropping every few minutes, and breakfast was a sad buffet with rubbery eggs and cold coffee. Won't be returning to the Talbott.

Great location near midtown, but that's the only plus. The bathroom was grimy with mold in the shower, the room dusty, and constant street noise made sleeping nearly impossible. Disappointing overall.
Wifi kept dropping all week, the bathroom had mold in the shower corners, and the room never felt clean. Only plus was the location, right by the metro. Otherwise a big letdown.
Two nights here felt like a week. The decor is stuck in the 80s, the bathroom wasn't properly cleaned, and for what we paid it was a complete rip-off. Won't be back.
Dusty surfaces and a stained carpet set the tone, and street noise kept me up half the night. Breakfast was sparse and lukewarm. Barely slept two solid hours--would not stay again.

The harbor view was nice enough, but that's where the praise ends. Paper-thin walls meant hearing every neighbor all night, I barely slept, and the disinterested staff couldn't have cared less. Expected far more from Conrad.

For nearly $600 a night I expected far more than a dated bathroom with a dripping shower and walls so thin I heard every hallway conversation. Great location downtown, but definitely not worth the price.
Dated, tired decor and a noisy street view that faced a parking lot. Breakfast was a sad cold buffet--stale pastries and watery eggs. Definitely not worth the price.
Barely slept thanks to a clunky, creaky bed, and the room felt straight out of the 90s. Bathroom had mold in the grout; my 'city view' was mostly a concrete wall. Wouldn't return.
Two nights here felt like a week--the wifi barely loaded anything, the shower dripped all night, and breakfast was cold eggs and stale pastries. Would not stay again.
Shower barely had hot water and the bathroom felt grimy. Street noise kept me up half the night, so I slept terribly, and breakfast was cold and stale. Not worth the price at all.

The Intercontinental's tired decor and a musty, poorly cleaned room made our three-night stay drag on far too long, plus constant hallway noise meant we barely slept. Expected much better at this price.

Sadly disappointing stay at Hotel James. Walls were paper-thin--I heard every hallway conversation all night, making my two days feel endless. WiFi constantly dropped, and the location was far from anything worth visiting.

Disappointing stay at the Knickerbocker. Traffic noise kept me up all night despite requesting a quiet room, staff seemed indifferent at check-in, and while Times Square location is convenient, I won't be returning.

Disappointing stay at the Monaco. Our room overlooked a dingy alley, the decor felt stuck in the 90s, and hallway noise kept us up both nights. Couldn't wait to check out--two nights felt like a week.
Desk staff acted like we were an inconvenience, and our 'city view' window faced a brick wall. Worse, the street noise kept me up all night despite earplugs--barely slept at all. Won't return.
Sadly not worth the price at all. Our room had dusty surfaces and a grimy bathroom with moldy grout, and the staff were dismissive whenever we raised issues. Won't be returning.

The location was convenient for sightseeing, but that's the only positive. My room had a stale smell and dusty carpet, the bathroom fixtures were rusty, and the 'view' was just a brick wall. Disappointing overall.
Such a letdown for a Sofitel--the bathroom had cracked tiles and weak water pressure, the decor felt stuck in the 90s, and the location wasn't walkable to anything. One night honestly felt too long.

Disappointed with my stay: paper-thin walls meant constant hallway noise, the wifi kept dropping, and I barely slept. The room was ostensibly clean, but stains on the carpet said otherwise. Not worth the price.
For nearly $400 a night I expected far more--tired, dated decor, a room that never felt truly clean, and street noise that wrecked my sleep both nights. Disappointing overall.
Thin walls meant I heard every hallway conversation til 2am, and the 'suite' felt tired and musty. Front desk was polite but slow. For the price, I expected way more. Not staying here again.

Disappointing stay overall. Room smelled musty, the AC barely cooled, and housekeeping skipped our floor twice. Front desk staff were indifferent when we complained. Location was fine, but I won't be back.
Honestly expected more from Hotel Amalfi. The view was nice, sure, but the room smelled musty and the AC barely worked, and staff took ages to answer anything. Wouldn't stay again.

Honestly pretty underwhelmed by the Hotel Ambassador. The room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and front desk barely acknowledged us at check-in. For what we paid, expected way more. Won't be back.
Honestly underwhelmed for the price. Booked the Conrad expecting luxury but got a room with a broken AC, slow service at breakfast, and street noise all night. Wouldn't return.
Disappointing stay at the Fairmont. Our room wasn't ready at check-in, the AC barely worked, and housekeeping skipped our floor one day entirely. For the price, expected far better service.

Expected way more from the Hard Rock. The music theme is fun for about five minutes until you realize the walls are paper thin and the bar noise carries all night. Room was tired, AC rattled, staff seemed annoyed we even asked for anything. Won't be back.

Disappointing stay at the Hilton. Room wasn't ready at check-in, the air conditioning barely worked, and staff seemed indifferent to my complaints. Expected much more for the price. Won't be returning.
Honestly disappointed with Homewood. My room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and the 'hot' breakfast was lukewarm at best. Front desk took forever to answer. Won't be returning.
Expected more from a Hyatt. Room smelled musty, walls were thin, and the front desk took forever to fix our broken AC. Location was fine but honestly won't be rushing back.

Sad to say the InterContinental didn't live up to the photos. My room smelled musty, housekeeping skipped my floor one day, and the front desk took ages to sort a billing error. For the price, very underwhelming.

Expected more from the James. My room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping skipped my floor entirely one day. Staff were pleasant enough but the value just wasn't there. Won't be returning.

Disappointed with the Knickerbocker. Paid a fortune for a room that felt dated, and the AC rattled all night. Location is fine, but at these rates I expected far better service and much quieter rooms. Won't be back.
Expected way more from the Monaco. The room smelled stale, the AC rattled all night, and front desk took forever to answer. For the price, honestly a letdown.
Disappointing stay at the Omni. Our room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping skipped us entirely one day. For the price, I expected far more--probably won't be back.

Disappointed with the Palmer. Our room smelled musty, the AC barely worked, and housekeeping skipped us one day entirely. Front desk staff were indifferent when we complained. For the price, expected far better. Won't be back.

Disappointing stay at the Sheraton. Check-in took forever, my room smelled musty, and the AC barely worked. Staff seemed indifferent when I mentioned it. For the price, I expected much better. Won't be back.

Honestly disappointed with the Sofitel. Paid for a premium room and got a view of the air shaft, air conditioning that rattled all night, and front desk staff who couldn't care less when I complained. Won't be back.
Expected more from Swissotel. The room felt tired and the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping barely showed up. Location is fine, but for this price I won't be returning.

For a hotel at this price point, the Talbott was a letdown. The room felt tired and dated, the noise from the street kept us up half the night, and staff service was indifferent at best. Probably won't be back.

Disappointing stay at the Affinia. Room was dated with a musty smell, the AC barely worked, and front desk staff seemed indifferent when we complained. Price felt way too high for what we got. Won't return.
Disappointing stay overall -- room smelled musty, the AC barely worked, and staff seemed annoyed whenever we asked for anything. For the price, I expected much better. Won't be returning.
Disappointing stay overall. Rooms felt tired and dated, the AC barely worked, and staff were indifferent when we raised it. For the price, expected far better from a hotel in such a great location.

Expected much more from the Hotel Ambassador. The room smelled stale, the air conditioning barely worked, and the front desk staff seemed annoyed by every request. Breakfast was cold and overpriced. Won't be returning.

Expected more from the Conrad. Room felt dated for the price, and housekeeping skipped our floor twice. Front desk was polite but slow. GREAT location though--sadly that's the only highlight of our stay.

Expected much more from the Fairmont. Our room wasn't ready at check-in, the staff seemed disinterested, and the pool area was crowded and noisy. For the price, honestly a pretty disappointing stay overall.
Disappointing stay at the Hard Rock. Rooms felt dated and the AC barely worked, plus check-in took forever. For the price, I expected way better music-themed fun than a noisy, tired hotel.
Disappointing stay at this Hilton -- the room smelled musty, the AC barely worked, and front desk staff were indifferent when I complained. For the price, I expected far better. Won't be returning.
Disappointing stay. The room smelled musty, the AC barely worked, and the 'free breakfast' was cold and picked over by 8am. Front desk staff were indifferent at check-in too. Won't be back.
Disappointing stay at the Hyatt. Room wasn't ready at check-in, AC barely worked, and staff seemed indifferent when we mentioned it. Expected way more for the price.
Expected so much more from an InterContinental. Room was dusty, AC barely worked, and staff took hours to fix it. Overpriced for this level of service--won't be returning.
Room was musty and the AC barely worked, front desk took an hour to check us in. Breakfast was basically cold eggs and stale bread. For this price, honestly expected way more. Won't be back.
Expected more from the Knickerbocker. Tiny room, noisy AC, and the front desk staff acted like we were an inconvenience. For $700 a night, honestly disappointing. Won't be back.
Not worth the hype at all. Our room smelled musty, the AC barely worked, and housekeeping skipped our floor twice. For the price we paid, the Monaco felt tired and understaffed. Won't be back.

Expected much more from the Omni. Our room smelled stale, the air conditioning barely worked, and front desk staff seemed annoyed every time we asked for anything. For the price, honestly a real letdown.
Disappointing stay at the Hotel Palmer. Room smelled musty, the AC barely worked, and front desk staff seemed annoyed every time we asked a question. Definitely not worth the price.
Disappointing stay at the Sheraton--check-in took forever, the room smelled musty, and the AC barely worked. For the price, I expected much better. Probably won't be back.
Expected far more from a Sofitel. Room felt tired, AC barely worked, and staff were indifferent at best. The so-called luxury price bought us noise until 2am and a mediocre breakfast. Won't be back.

Disappointing stay at the Swissotel. Room was dated with a stained carpet, check-in took forever, and the 'luxury' breakfast was cold and overpriced. Staff seemed indifferent throughout. Expected far more for this price.
Expected much more from the Talbott. Our room felt dated and the AC barely worked, staff took ages to fix it. Not worth the price at all. Disappointing stay.

I stayed at the Affinia for four nights on a work trip and honestly wish it had been longer. The location made getting around easy, and the room was a genuine surprise--much bigger than I expected, with a kitchenette that came in handy more than once. What really stood out was how quiet it was. My room faced an interior side, so even with the windows open I barely heard street noise, and I slept solidly every night on what I'd call one of the more comfortable hotel beds I've encountered. The free wifi was fast and reliable throughout, which mattered since I had video calls most mornings. Staff were friendly without being overbearing, and housekeeping was consistent. If I'm back in the city, this is where I'll book. A few small scuffs on the furniture, but nothing that dented a great stay.

I stayed at the Hotel Allegro for three nights over a long weekend and came away really impressed. The room was spotless when I checked in, and housekeeping kept it that way throughout my stay, even restocking the coffee pods without being asked. I'm a light sleeper, but the bed was genuinely comfortable and the street noise was barely noticeable, so I got solid rest every night. The decor has that classic 1920s theater-district character with rich colors and vintage touches, but it felt freshly updated rather than dated, which I appreciated. Wifi was fast and reliable, no dropped connections even while streaming in the evenings. The front desk team was warm and quick with dinner recommendations. Would absolutely book here again next time I'm in Chicago.

We stayed at the Hotel Amalfi for four nights in early September and it genuinely exceeded what I expected for the price. I was a little worried the area would be noisy at night, but the windows block out almost everything, and we slept quietly the whole stay. The room itself was spotless, honestly one of the cleanest I've seen, housekeeping even arranged our toiletries neatly each day. Wifi was fast and stable, my husband worked from the room two mornings with video calls and never had a lag issue. Breakfast surprised us: fresh pastries, decent espresso, eggs, fruit, and they happily made adjustments when I asked. The rooftop views weren't the selling point I thought they'd be, but the staff made up for it with warm, unhurried service. We'd happily come back next trip.

We stayed at the Ambassador for three nights in early October and were thoroughly impressed. Our room on the sixth floor was spotless when we checked in, not a dust mote or stray hair anywhere, and housekeeping kept it that way throughout our visit. The bathroom was surprisingly roomy, with a deep tub, strong water pressure, and fluffy towels replaced daily without our even having to ask. I was a little worried the decor might feel tired given the hotel's age, but the recent renovation shows: fresh paint, updated light fixtures, and a nice mix of classic and contemporary touches. Best of all, the beds are genuinely comfortable with firm mattresses and quality pillows, so I slept better than I do at home. Location near the park was a bonus. Would happily return.

We stayed at the Conrad for four nights and I honestly can't find much to fault. The front desk team remembered our names after the first morning and even mailed back a charger we left behind in the lobby. Breakfast was a highlight: fresh pastries, made-to-order eggs, and strong coffee that rivaled the place around the corner. Our room on the 20th floor was remarkably quiet despite being in the middle of everything; once the door closed, we heard nothing but the hum of the AC. Wifi stayed fast and reliable throughout, which mattered since my husband had to join a few video calls. Housekeeping deserves a shout-out too. It's not the cheapest option in town, but we felt it was worth every cent and would happily return.

We spent three nights at the Fairmont and honestly wished it had been a week. Our room on a high floor was remarkably quiet -- even with the elevator bank nearby, we never heard a thing, and both of us slept soundly through the night, which almost never happens for me in hotels. The bed was plush without being too soft, and the blackout curtains did their job well. Wifi was included and fast enough that I took a video call one morning with zero issues. Housekeeping kept everything spotless, and the concierge booked us a dinner reservation that turned out to be the highlight of the trip. The location near the water made evening walks easy. Would absolutely return, and next time for longer.

We stayed at the Hard Rock for three nights during a concert weekend and honestly it exceeded what I expected for the rate. Check-in took a few minutes and the front desk guy even gave us a tip about avoiding the elevator crowds after shows, which saved us time twice. Our room faced away from the street so it was remarkably quiet given how lively the lobby gets at night -- we slept fine even with a party happening downstairs. The music memorabilia everywhere gets a bit touristy, but that's part of the charm. Breakfast was included in our package: solid buffet with fresh fruit, made-to-order omelets, and decent coffee that got refilled without asking. The staff overall seemed genuinely happy to help, not just going through the motions. For the location and quality, I'd call it worth the money. Would book again.

I stayed at the Hilton for three nights on a work trip and came away genuinely impressed, which I wasn't expecting at this price point. My room was on the fourteenth floor, and the view looking out over the city at dusk was the kind of thing you stop unpacking to stare at. The bathroom was spotless and bigger than I'd anticipated, with strong water pressure and fluffy towels restocked without my even asking. Every staff member I crossed paths with, from the front desk to the breakfast crew, seemed to actually enjoy their jobs and greeted me by name after the first day. The lobby and rooms have been recently refreshed, so nothing felt tired or dated the way some older chains do. Only tiny gripe was slow elevator waits at checkout time, but that's a crowd problem, not a quality problem. I'd happily return.

We stayed at the Homewood Suites for four nights and honestly couldn't have asked for a better value. The rate was noticeably lower than comparable hotels nearby, yet we got far more than we expected. Our room was spotless when we checked in, and housekeeping kept it that way throughout our visit, even restocking coffee supplies without being asked. The bathroom, while not huge, was in great shape with strong water pressure and a shower that heated up in seconds. Best part was the sleep quality: the bed was firm but comfortable, the pillows were fluffy, and despite being near the elevator we never heard a thing once the door closed. With a hot breakfast thrown in every morning, this place easily beats anything else we've stayed at in this price range. We'll definitely be back.

I stayed at the Grand Hyatt for four nights on a work trip and came away genuinely impressed. My room on the 22nd floor was quiet enough that I slept through the night every single time, which almost never happens for me in hotels -- the bed was firm but comfortable and the blackout curtains actually did their job. The bathroom was a highlight: large walk-in shower with strong water pressure, plenty of counter space, and they restocked towels without my even having to ask. Decor-wise, everything felt fresh and recently updated, with warm lighting and modern fixtures rather than the tired gold-and-maroon look some older Hyatts still have. It isn't cheap, but between the location next to the transit stop, the helpful front desk, and the quality of the room itself, I felt the price was fair and would happily return.

We stayed at the InterContinental for three nights and honestly wished we'd booked a full week. Our room on the 21st floor was spotless, not a stray hair or smudge anywhere, and housekeeping kept it that way without us ever having to ask twice. The view over the city skyline was spectacular, especially at dusk when all the lights came on. The bed was comfortable, though I'd expect nothing less at this price point. Wifi was fast and reliable throughout, which mattered since I had to hop on a couple of video calls from the room and never had a single dropout. Breakfast was excellent too. A few small bumps at check-in with the room not being ready, but nothing that soured the experience. Would absolutely return.

We stayed at the James for three nights in mid-October and left genuinely impressed. The location is hard to beat -- a short walk to the Magnificent Mile, but tucked on a quiet side street so you don't get the constant street noise. Our room was spotless when we arrived, and housekeeping kept it that way throughout the stay, restocking towels and coffee without being asked. The bathroom was a highlight: generous counter space, a deep soaking tub, and those Kiehl's products my wife kept raving about. What really made the stay, though, was the staff. The front desk teammate who checked us in remembered our names after the first night, and the concierge sorted out dinner reservations twice with zero attitude. Would absolutely return next time we're in Chicago.

We spent four nights at the Knickerbocker and were genuinely impressed. Even though the hotel sits right on Broadway, our room on a higher floor was remarkably quiet--I honestly never heard street noise once, which is rare in midtown. The view from our window looked out over the rooftops toward Times Square, and watching the city light up at dusk never got old. Housekeeping kept everything spotless; the bathroom gleamed and the linens smelled fresh every day. The staff went out of their way for us too--doormen greeted us by name by the second day, and the front desk arranged a late checkout without any fuss when our flight changed. One small note: the elevator can get a bit crowded at peak hours, but that's a minor quibble. Would absolutely stay again.

We stayed at the Monaco for three nights in early October and I'm still thinking about it. I'd read some mixed comments about noise before booking, so I requested a room away from the street, and the front desk looked after us without any fuss. It turned out to be genuinely quiet the whole stay, which honestly made the trip. The location is hard to beat if you're on foot: grab a coffee and you're at the waterfront in ten minutes, museums and restaurants just a short walk in the other direction. Our room had the quirks you'd expect from a boutique property, but everything worked, including the wifi, which stayed fast even when the place filled up for a conference midweek. The bathroom was bigger than we needed, with good water pressure and decent toiletries. Staff remembered our names by day two. Would return without hesitation.

Our three-night stay at the Omni was exactly what we needed after months of planning this trip. We were on the fourteenth floor, and the view alone was worth the upgrade I requested at booking--waking up to streetlights and rooftops stretching out toward the mountains each morning felt like a small luxury. Despite being so high up in a busy part of downtown, the room was remarkably quiet; we heard only a faint rumble of an occasional elevator two doors down, and absolutely nothing once we closed the curtains at night. I'm a light sleeper, so this mattered enormously, and I slept eight solid hours every night without waking once. The bathroom pleasantly surprised me too, with a deep tub, strong water pressure, and plush towels replenished daily. The housekeeping staff even folded my daughter's stuffed animal into a little chair one afternoon, which made her whole trip. We'd return here without hesitation.

I stayed at the Hotel Palmer for three nights in early October and was genuinely impressed. The lobby and rooms have been recently renovated, so everything felt fresh and modern rather than the tired, dated look you sometimes get at this price point. My room on the sixth floor faced an interior courtyard, which kept things remarkably quiet despite the busy street outside--I slept better there than I do at home, honestly. The front desk staff were warm without being overbearing; when I asked about a late checkout they arranged it in under a minute, no fuss. Breakfast was included and better than expected: fresh fruit, decent pastries, eggs cooked to order, and good coffee that someone actually refilled promptly. Only minor quibble was slow elevator service at peak times. Would gladly return.

We stayed at the Sheraton over a long weekend and honestly I wish it had been longer. From the moment we arrived, the staff went out of their way to make things easy -- the front desk upgraded us when they could, and the concierge spent twenty minutes marking up a map with restaurant suggestions that turned out to be spot on. Our room on the fourteenth floor looked straight out over the river, and watching the boats go by at night with the city lights up was worth the price of the room on its own. The bed was genuinely comfortable, housekeeping was prompt and thorough, and everything felt well maintained without being stuffy. It's not the cheapest hotel in town, but given the location and the little touches, we felt we got real value. Already looking at dates to come back.

We stayed at the Sofitel for four nights and honestly, it felt far too short. From the moment we arrived, the staff went out of their way to make everything easy -- the concierge booked us a last-minute dinner reservation and the front desk remembered our names by day two. Our room on the fourteenth floor looked straight out over the city, and watching the sunset from the window with a glass of wine became our nightly ritual. Breakfast was a proper event: fresh pastries, made-to-order eggs, and a spread of fruit and cheeses that changed slightly every morning. Even the little touches, like turndown service and the doorman hailing cabs within seconds, made the experience feel effortless. We're already planning to return for a full week.

We spent three nights at the Swissotel and honestly wished it could have been longer. The staff stood out most to me -- the front desk upgraded our room without being asked, and the concierge was never pushy, just genuinely helpful when we asked about dinner spots nearby. The room itself was sleek and considerably more generous than I expected from a big chain tower, and the bathroom was a real highlight: granite counter, deep soaking tub, and water pressure that actually deserves the word 'powerful.' Given the river views and the location right near the Loop, the price felt fair, maybe even a bargain compared to some competitors. Sunday checkout was smooth and unhurried. If we get back to Chicago, this is where we'll stay again.

I stayed at the Talbott for four nights in early October and would happily return. The location turned out to be ideal, quiet residential street feel yet only a short walk to Michigan Avenue shopping and plenty of restaurants nearby. My room was spotless when I arrived, and housekeeping kept it that way throughout my stay, right down to the neatly folded towels each afternoon. Despite being in the middle of the city, I never heard noise from the hallway or the street once the windows were closed, and I slept better than I do at home. What really set the place apart, though, was the staff. Everyone from the front desk to the doormen was warm and genuinely attentive without being intrusive. The bellman even gave me walking directions with a hand-drawn map. A solid, comfortable stay all around.

I stayed at the Affinia for a four-night business trip and was genuinely pleased with the experience. The location is hard to beat--just a couple of blocks from the subway and walking distance to plenty of restaurants, which made getting around effortless. I'd read mixed things about the rooms online, but mine felt fresh and well maintained, with updated furnishings and a comfortable bed rather than anything dated. The view wasn't anything dramatic since I faced a side street, but it was quiet and bright during the day, which I appreciated. Wifi worked reliably the whole time, even during video calls, with no annoying dropouts or login hassles. Staff were friendly and check-in took two minutes. Would absolutely book again for my next visit.

We stayed at the Allegro for three nights in mid-June and honestly didn't want to leave. Our room on the fifth floor looked out over the harbor, and watching the boats come in with morning coffee became the highlight of each day. The decor is fresh and modern, warm wood tones and soft lighting rather than the tired floral drapes you still get in so many places. Breakfast exceeded expectations: fresh pastries, made-to-order eggs, good coffee, and plenty of fruit and yogurt options. What really stood out, though, was the staff. The front desk remembered our names by the second day, and when I asked for a late checkout they arranged it without any fuss. Friendly without being pushy, attentive without hovering. We'll definitely be back next year.

We stayed at Hotel Amalfi for four nights in early June and genuinely didn't want to leave. The room was spotless, housekeeping seemed to appear at exactly the right moments, and the beds were surprisingly comfortable for a coastal hotel, so we slept soundly every night despite the church bells in the morning. The staff deserve special mention; the front desk arranged a last-minute boat tour for us and the breakfast team remembered our coffee order by day two. As for the view, waking up to terraced lemon groves tumbling down toward the sea never got old, and the rooftop terrace at sunset was simply breathtaking. Yes, it's on the pricier side, but for the location, service, and those balcony views, we felt it was absolutely worth it. Would return in a heartbeat.

We stayed at Hotel Ambassador for four nights and left thoroughly pleased. Our room faced the courtyard side, so despite the central location we heard almost nothing at night -- genuinely quiet, and we slept well every evening. From the small balcony on the upper floors you can catch a glimpse of the rooftops toward the old town, nothing dramatic, but charming at sunset. The location really is the hotel's trump card: the metro stop is a two-minute walk, and restaurants and a pharmacy are right around the corner. Staff were consistently warm without being overbearing -- the front desk arranged an early check-in without fuss, and the breakfast team remembered our coffee order by the second morning. Small touches like the fresh fruit in the room made it feel cared for. Would happily return.

We booked the Conrad for our anniversary weekend and honestly expected it to be lovely, but it still exceeded our expectations, which made the price feel completely worth it. Our room on a high floor was spacious and beautifully maintained, and the bathroom was a genuine highlight -- huge soaking tub, separate rain shower, marble everywhere, and fluffy towels restocked twice a day. The wifi was fast and reliable; I had a video call one morning with zero glitches. Best of all, despite being in the middle of everything, the room was remarkably quiet. We barely heard a sound from the hall or the street, and we slept better than we do at home. Staff remembered our names by day two. We'll absolutely be back for our next special occasion.

I stayed at the Fairmont for three nights and honestly can't fault it. My room was spotless, housekeeping kept everything immaculate each day, and the little touches like fresh linens and a properly made bed made a real difference. The bathroom was a highlight, spacious marble finishes, strong water pressure, and those fluffy robes I ended up living in. Sleep quality was excellent too; the bed was firm but comfortable and the blackout curtains blocked out the city light completely. Yes, it's pricey, but for the level of service, the impeccable concierge, and the overall standard, I'd say it's absolutely worth treating yourself. The staff remembered my name by day two, which felt genuinely welcoming. Would book again without hesitation next time I'm in town.

We stayed at the Hard Rock for three nights and honestly it exceeded our expectations. The room was spotless when we arrived and housekeeping kept it that way throughout our stay, even replacing towels before we asked. The wifi was fast and reliable, which mattered since I had to join a couple of video calls from the room with no buffering at all. The bathroom was a pleasant surprise, actually spacious, with good water pressure and plenty of counter space for two people getting ready in the morning. Despite being right in the middle of everything, our room was impressively quiet at night, we never heard noise from the hallway or the street below. The rock-and-roll decor is fun without being gimmicky. Would absolutely book again on our next trip.

We stayed at the Hilton for three nights while visiting family downtown, and the location couldn't have been more convenient--everything we wanted to see was within easy walking distance, and the airport shuttle ran like clockwork. Our room on the fourteenth floor was nicely updated; the decor felt fresh and modern, none of the tired, dated furnishings you sometimes find in big chains. Wi-Fi was fast and reliable the whole time, which mattered since my husband had to join a couple of video calls. Even better, it was remarkably quiet despite being right in the busy part of town--we slept soundly with the blackout curtains closed. Staff at the front desk and breakfast lounge were genuinely friendly. Would happily return on our next trip; it checked every box we cared about.

We stayed at Homewood for four nights and were genuinely pleased with the whole experience. The location couldn't have been more convenient -- a short walk to the train station, restaurants, and the main shopping street, which made getting around effortless. The wifi worked reliably throughout our stay, strong enough in the room for video calls and streaming without a single dropout, which is rare in my experience. The staff were warm and helpful without being overbearing; when we asked for a late checkout on our last day, they arranged it with no fuss and even printed our boarding passes. Considering the nightly rate included a solid breakfast with fresh options and free parking, it absolutely felt worth the price. Would happily return and recommend it to friends visiting the area.

We stayed four nights at the Hyatt and honestly wished it could have been a week. From check-in, the staff went out of their way to make us feel welcome--the front desk agent remembered our names the entire stay, and the concierge arranged a last-minute dinner reservation without blinking. Our room on the 14th floor had a floor-to-ceiling window overlooking the harbor, and waking up to that skyline every morning was worth the trip alone. The decor felt fresh rather than dated; warm woods, crisp linens, and lighting that actually worked instead of the usual hotel gloom. Housekeeping was prompt and thorough. If I had one quibble, it's that our trip felt far too short to enjoy the pool and lounge properly. We'll be back for a longer stay.

I stayed at the InterContinental for three nights and honestly wish it had been a week. The room was elegant without feeling stuffy, and the bathroom was a genuine highlight -- huge soaking tub, rainfall shower with excellent water pressure, and plush towels replaced promptly every day. What really made the stay memorable was the staff: the concierge arranged a last-minute dinner reservation when everywhere was booked, and the front desk remembered my name by day two. Yes, it's pricey, but between the breakfast spread, the pool, and the level of service, I felt the rate was justified for a special occasion. Checkout was smooth and they held our bags courteously. Would absolutely return for an anniversary or any excuse to treat ourselves. Highly recommended.

I stayed at Hotel James for three nights and honestly slept better than I do at home. The bed was plush without being too soft, and despite being right in the city center, my room on the fifth floor facing the courtyard was remarkably quiet -- no street noise, no hallway commotion, even on a Friday night. Breakfast exceeded my expectations: fresh pastries, proper coffee, eggs cooked to order, and enough variety that I never got bored. Location-wise, it's hard to beat, just a five-minute walk to the main square with restaurants and the tram stop practically at the doorstep. Staff were warm and helpful with directions whenever I asked. Small imperfections like a slow bathroom drain aside, I'd happily return and recommend it to anyone visiting.

We spent three nights at the Knickerbocker and honestly wish it had been a week. The room was spotless when we arrived, housekeeping kept it that way throughout, and the bed was genuinely comfortable after long days of walking around the city. Location is hard to beat, tucked right off Times Square yet surprisingly quiet once the door closes, with the subway a couple minutes away. Breakfast in the restaurant was a highlight each morning, fresh pastries, excellent coffee, and eggs cooked to order rather than the usual buffet tray. Staff were warm without hovering. Would happily return.

We stayed at the Hotel Monaco for three nights and honestly wished it could have been a full week. The room was spotless when we checked in, and housekeeping kept it that way throughout our visit, which is not something we say often. The bed was genuinely comfortable, and between the quiet hallway and the blackout curtains, I slept better than I do at home. Breakfast was a highlight each morning: fresh pastries, good coffee, and eggs that were actually hot instead of sitting under a heat lamp. The staff greeted us by name by the second day. Location is walkable to plenty of restaurants and shops. We left feeling rested and well taken care of, and we will absolutely be back next time we're in town. Highly recommend.

We stayed at the Omni for three nights over a long weekend, and honestly, it exceeded what I expected for the price. Yes, it's not the cheapest option in the city, but between the location, the service, and the quality of the room, I felt like we got real value. Our room had been recently refurbished, so the decor felt fresh and modern, nothing dated or tired like some photos suggested. The bed was genuinely comfortable, and the housekeeping staff kept everything spotless. Breakfast was a highlight: a hot buffet with made-to-order omelets, fresh fruit, and really good coffee, served in a bright, pleasant dining room. One small gripe: the wifi was spotty in the corner of our room near the window, though it worked fine everywhere else. Would happily return.

I stayed at the Hotel Palmer for three nights in early October and was genuinely impressed. The bed was incredibly comfortable--firm mattress, plush pillows--and I slept soundly every night despite the central location. The bathroom was spotless and recently renovated, with a rain shower that had excellent water pressure and plenty of hot water, plus nice toiletries. Breakfast exceeded my expectations: fresh pastries, real fruit, good coffee, and made-to-order eggs rather than the usual sad buffet fare. Staff were friendly without being intrusive. Considering how central it is and the quality of everything, the price felt very reasonable. I'd happily book again on my next visit and would recommend it to anyone wanting solid comfort without paying boutique-hotel prices. Overall a very satisfying stay.

We stayed at the Sheraton for three nights and were genuinely impressed. Our room on the twelfth floor had a gorgeous view of the harbor, and watching the sunset from the window each evening became the highlight of our day. The room itself was spotless--housekeeping even left fresh towels twice a day without being asked. The bed was wonderfully comfortable with plush pillows, and the blackout curtains meant I slept straight through the night, which almost never happens for me when traveling. Every staff member we encountered, from the front desk to the breakfast team, was warm and attentive; when I mentioned I preferred extra coffee packets, they appeared the next morning without a reminder. Location was convenient too, just a short walk from the metro. Would absolutely return next time we're in the city.

We stayed at the Sofitel for three nights and honestly wished it had been a week. The bed was wonderful -- the mattress had that perfect balance of firmness and softness, and with the blackout curtains I slept straight through every night without waking once, which almost never happens for me. Even better, the room was remarkably quiet despite the hotel being fully booked; we heard no hallway noise or street traffic at all, just the distant hum of the air conditioning. The wifi was fast and reliable throughout, easily handling video calls and streaming in the evenings without a single drop. Staff were warm and attentive from check-in to checkout, and the breakfast spread was excellent. Highly recommend and we'll definitely be back.

We stayed at the Swissotel for four nights last month, and while it's not cheap, I genuinely felt we got our money's worth given the location and the quality of everything. Our room was on a higher floor and the view over the city at sunset was absolutely stunning--we found ourselves just sitting by the window with coffee every evening. What really stood out, though, was the staff. Check-in was smooth, and when we asked for a late checkout the front desk handled it graciously without any hassle. The breakfast team remembered our preferences by the second morning, which felt like a nice personal touch. Wifi was fast and reliable throughout, even during a video call I had to take one afternoon. Would happily return.

We stayed at the Talbott for four nights in October and were genuinely impressed. Our room on the fourteenth floor was beautifully refreshed -- the furnishings, bedding, and bathroom all felt recently renovated, nothing dated about it at all. Sleep quality was excellent; the bed was plush but supportive, blackout curtains worked perfectly, and despite being so close to Rush Street we barely heard any street noise, just the occasional distant siren. The wifi was free and fast enough for video calls I had to take for work, with no drops during my stay. Housekeeping was prompt and thorough. Location is unbeatable for shopping and dining, and the staff remembered my coffee order by day two. Would happily return for our next Chicago trip without hesitation.

We stayed at the Affinia for a long weekend and it turned out to be one of the better hotel experiences we've had in the city. Our room was huge for downtown, with a separate seating area and a kitchenette that came in handy for late-night snacks. The bed was genuinely comfortable, which matters a lot to me since I usually sleep badly in hotels. What really stood out was the staff, though. When our heating wasn't working right the first evening, someone came up within ten minutes and fixed it, and the front desk called later just to confirm everything was okay. That kind of follow-through is rare. Location is convenient too, easy walk to Michigan Avenue and plenty of restaurants nearby. Not fancy in a pretentious way, just solid, comfortable, and well run. We'd absolutely come back.

We stayed at the Allegro for four nights in October and it honestly exceeded what I expected from a downtown property at this price. The location is fantastic -- a short walk to the theatres on Randolph and easy access to the L, but the room faced away from the street so we slept without hearing trains or traffic. The bed was genuinely comfortable, and the shower had good water pressure, which I always notice more than people probably should. One small hiccup with our room key deactivating twice, but the front desk fixed it in a minute each time and even apologized with a couple of free drink vouchers. Everything about the place has a fun, slightly jazz-era vibe without feeling gimmicky. Would happily come back next time we're in the city.

We stayed at Hotel Amalfi for four nights in early June and honestly could not have asked for a better base for exploring the coast. Our room on the third floor had a small balcony with a view that made getting up early feel like less of a chore. Breakfast was included and the pastries alone were worth it, plus the woman working the coffee machine remembered how I liked my cappuccino by day two, which is the kind of thing that matters. Front desk staff booked us a boat trip to Capri last minute and gave honest advice about which restaurants were tourist traps. The walk up from the beach is steep, but that's Amalfi in general, not the hotel's fault. Would happily return.

We stayed at the Hotel Ambassador for four nights in October and were genuinely impressed. Our room on the sixth floor overlooked the courtyard, so even though the street below gets lively at night, we slept like logs. Beds here deserve a mention -- the mattress was firm but comfortable, and the pillows actually stayed cool. Front desk staff were quick with restaurant suggestions when we asked, sending us to a tiny bistro two blocks away that ended up being the best meal of the trip. Housekeeping was thorough and came when scheduled without us having to chase anyone down. Breakfast had a decent spread, though the coffee could be stronger. Only real hiccup was a slow elevator one morning, minor stuff. Would happily book here again.

We stayed at the Conrad for four nights over a long weekend and honestly I can't think of a single complaint. Our room on a high floor had a genuinely impressive view of the city skyline at night, and the bed was so comfortable I actually looked up where they buy their mattresses (turns out some things you just can't order). Housekeeping was discreet and spot-on every day. The location worked out better than expected since we could walk to a ton of restaurants and it's a short ride to the museums. One small thing that stood out was the front desk calling to check if our room was fine an hour after check-in, which has never happened to me anywhere else. Not the cheapest option in the city, but for an anniversary trip it was absolutely worth it. Would return without hesitation.

We stayed at the Fairmont for four nights over a long weekend and honestly have very few complaints. Our room on a higher floor had a gorgeous view of the mountains and the water, and the bed was one of the most comfortable I've ever slept in at a hotel - I actually looked up the mattress brand before checking out. Housekeeping was prompt and thorough every day, and the front desk straightened out a small billing mix-up within minutes without any fuss. The pool area never felt crowded even though the hotel was fairly full, and the concierge booked us a last-minute dinner reservation at a place that turned out to be the highlight of our trip. Location is excellent too, an easy walk to everything we wanted to see. None of this is cheap, but you get what you pay for. We'd happily return.

We stayed at the Hard Rock for four nights over a long weekend and honestly it exceeded what I expected. The music theme could easily feel gimmicky but it's done well, memorabilia everywhere without being over the top. Our room was quiet despite being right off the main drag, the bed was genuinely comfortable, and the shower had great water pressure. Staff were consistently friendly, the front desk got us into a late checkout no problem, and the bartender down in the lobby bar made a killer old fashioned while a live acoustic set played. Location is solid too, walkable to a bunch of restaurants and nightlife. Only small gripe was slow elevator waits at peak times and valet taking a bit long one evening. Still, I'd book it again without hesitation. Great value for what we paid.

We stayed at the Hilton for four nights over a long weekend and honestly it exceeded what I expected. Our room on the 14th floor was spotless when we arrived, and housekeeping kept it that way every day without us ever having to ask twice. The bed was one of the most comfortable I've slept in at a hotel, big and soft with plenty of pillows, which is rare. Location-wise you can't beat it, we walked everywhere we wanted to go. The breakfast buffet was pricey but worth it once, and the executive lounge snacks saved us a few times. One small hiccup with the TV remote was fixed within ten minutes of calling the front desk. Check-in was quick and friendly, and the bell staff handled our luggage cheerfully. Would absolutely book again for our next trip.

We stayed at the Homewood for four nights over spring break and it ended up being one of the better hotel experiences we've had in a while. The complimentary breakfast actually had variety every morning, not the same sad bagels on repeat, and my kids went crazy for the waffle maker. Our room had a full kitchen, which sounds like a small thing but meant we could heat up leftovers and keep drinks cold without trekking downstairs. The bed was genuinely comfortable, none of that thin lumpy mattress stuff. Housekeeping came promptly when we asked for extra towels, and the front desk guy at night gave us a solid tip about a taco spot two blocks over. Free parking was a bonus in an area where most places charge big. Would book again without hesitation.

We stayed at the Hyatt for three nights over a long weekend and honestly I can't find much to complain about. The front desk upgraded us at check-in because they had the availability, which was a nice surprise after a delayed flight. Our room on the 14th floor faced the river, and watching the boats go by at night became my favorite little ritual. The bed was genuinely comfortable, not the usual too-soft hotel mattress, and the shower had real pressure. Housekeeping came early every day and even left extra coffee pods without being asked. Breakfast in the lobby restaurant ran a bit pricey, around $22 for eggs and toast, but the buffet was fresh and the waiter kept my cup full. Location worked out great too, we walked everywhere. Would happily book again.

We stayed at the InterContinental for four nights over a long weekend and honestly have very few complaints. Our room on a high floor had a great view of the river, and the bed was probably the most comfortable I've slept in at any hotel -- the pillows alone deserve a mention. Housekeeping kept everything spotless and even remembered our extra coffee request after the first morning. The club lounge was worth the upgrade, with decent snacks in the evening and a quiet place to work. Location is hard to beat too; we walked to most of what we wanted to see. Only minor gripe: the elevator wait could get long around breakfast hours. Front desk called up on our last day to confirm our late checkout without us even asking, which was a nice touch. Would happily return.

We stayed at the James for three nights over a long weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. The location puts you right in the middle of everything, we walked to dinner both nights and barely touched a cab. Our room wasn't huge but it was smartly laid out, and the bed might be the most comfortable I've slept in at any hotel, period. Housekeeping was quick and thorough, and when we asked for an extra blanket it showed up within ten minutes. The front desk staff were genuinely friendly without being overbearing, which is rarer than it should be. Small gripe: the elevator wait got a little long at peak times. That's really my only complaint though. Would absolutely book here again next time we're in town.

We stayed at the Knickerbocker for three nights over the holidays and I'm still thinking about it. The location is hard to beat -- Times Square is right there but somehow once you step inside the lobby you can't hear any of the madness. Our room was on a higher floor with a view down toward the intersection, which kept us entertained for longer than I'd like to admit. The bed was genuinely one of the most comfortable I've slept in at a hotel, and the shower had great water pressure, which I always appreciate. Breakfast at the restaurant downstairs was excellent -- the avocado toast and cappuccinos were worth getting up for. The staff went out of their way for us when we needed extra towels and a late checkout. Not a huge gym, but perfectly adequate. Would absolutely book this place again on our next trip to the city.

We stayed at the Monaco for three nights over a long weekend and it honestly exceeded what I was expecting. The location is fantastic, walkable to tons of restaurants and the waterfront, and the staff went out of their way to make us feel welcome, right down to remembering our names by the second day. Our room was on the smaller side but cleverly laid out, with a super comfortable bed and that quirky, colorful decor the brand does so well. Free wine hour in the evening was a nice touch we took advantage of twice. The only hiccup was a slow elevator situation on Saturday, but honestly with the vibe here I can't complain much. Housekeeping was thorough and quick. Would absolutely come back next time we're in town.

I stayed at the Omni for four nights over a long weekend and have zero complaints. The location is honestly hard to beat--everything I wanted to see was either walkable or a short rideshare away. Check-in was painless, and the bellman went out of his way to point out a fewlocal restaurants he personally liked, one of which turned out to be the best meal of the trip. My room was quiet despite being downtown, and the bed might be the most comfortable hotel bed I've slept in. Housekeeping kept everything spotless, and when I asked for extra coffee pods they were at my door within ten minutes. Breakfast in the restaurant one morning was solid, if a little pricey, but that's expected at this level. Would absolutely book here again next time I'm in town.

We stayed at the Hotel Palmer for three nights over a long weekend and honestly couldn't have asked for better. The location is ideal -- a short walk to the river and plenty of restaurants nearby without being in the middle of the noisy tourist strip. Our room was on the sixth floor, quiet, with a really comfortable bed that made sleeping in dangerously easy. The front desk staff went out of their way twice for us, once to print our train tickets and again when we asked where to find a good bakery in the morning (they pointed us to one two blocks over that was excellent). Breakfast buffet had a decent spread, nothing wild, but the coffee was actually good which matters more to me than it probably should. Small things: fast wifi, plenty of outlets by the bed, housekeeping was thorough. Would happily book again.

We stayed at the Sheraton for three nights over a long weekend and honestly had zero complaints. Our room on the 14th floor overlooked the river, which was a nice surprise since I hadn't requested a view. The bed was one of those plush ones with tons of pillows, and I actually slept better than I do at home. Housekeeping was consistent every day, and one evening they left extra towels without us even asking. The front desk upgraded us to the club level because of some mix-up with our room type, which normally would've been annoying but turned into a bonus -- free breakfast and snacks all day up there, plus a quiet place to escape the crowds. Location-wise it's an easy walk to basically everything downtown. Pool area got crowded Saturday afternoon but the kids loved it anyway. Would happily book here again next trip back.

We stayed at the Sofitel for three nights and it was honestly one of the better hotel experiences we've had in ages. The location is great, quiet street but still walkable to everything we wanted, and the moment you step into the lobby there's this calm, understated elegance that sets the tone. Our room on the ninth floor was spotless, the bed is genuinely one of the most comfortable I've slept in at any hotel, and the French touches like the bath products and the little welcome note made it feel special. Front desk staff remembered our names by day two, which was a nice surprise. Room service arrived faster than promised and the food was actually hot. Only tiny gripe would be slow elevator waits at peak times, but that's minor. Would absolutely return.

We stayed at the Swissotel over the Thanksgiving weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. Our room on a higher floor had an amazing view of the river and Lake Michigan, especially at night when everything lit up. The bed was genuinely comfortable, not one of those rock-hard hotel mattresses, and the blackout curtains actually did their job. What really made the trip was the front desk, who arranged a late checkout for us on the last day without any fuss. Location is unbeatable: you can walk to Millennium Park in about five minutes, ladies' number one tip is the Tomato Street restaurant downstairs for breakfast. Only small complaint is the elevators got a bit busy during peak hours. Would absolutely come back.

We stayed at the Talbott for a long weekend and it exceeded what I expected from the price point. It's a smaller boutique property, which I actually ended up loving, because the service felt personal rather than scripted. The doorman remembered our names by day two, and the front desk accommodated our late checkout without any hassle when our flight got pushed back. Rooms are European-sized, so on the cozy side, but the bedding was genuinely comfortable and everything was spotless. Location is hard to beat: quiet residential street feel off Rush, yet a short walk to Michigan Avenue and tons of restaurants. The free evening wine reception was a nice touch after a day of walking around. Only quibble is the elevator situation during busy times, but honestly it wouldn't stop me from returning. Solid choice.

We stayed at the Affinia for a long weekend and honestly had a great time. Check-in was quick despite us arriving early, and the front desk guy even mentioned they'd try to get us into a room right away, which they did. The room itself was bigger than expected for a city hotel, with a little kitchenette that came in handy for leftover pizza and morning coffee. Beds were comfortable, though the pillows were a bit soft for my taste, so I asked for a firmer one and housekeeping brought it up within ten minutes. Location was solid, plenty of food options nearby and easy access to the subway. One tiny thing: the hallway elevator wait could stretch a bit at peak times, but nothing that ruined anything. Would happily come back next trip.
