We stayed at Hotel Allegro for three nights in October and honestly it exceeded our expectations. Location is great, just a short walk from the main square but on a quiet side street, so no noise at night. Our room was spacious, spotlessly clean, and the bed was genuinely comfortable, which is rare in my experience. Breakfast was the highlight really: fresh pastries, good coffee, eggs made to order, and the staff kept everything stocked even when it got busy. Speaking of staff, everyone we interacted with was warm and helpful, and reception arranged us a taxi on the last day without any fuss. Minor quibble: the elevator is small and a bit slow, but nothing that would put me off returning. Good value overall. Highly recommended.

We stayed four nights at Hotel Amalfi and honestly didn't want to leave. Our room wasn't huge but it was spotless, with a small balcony overlooking the water that made morning coffee feel like a religious experience. The breakfast spread was better than expected -- fresh pastries, good espresso, and fruit that actually tasted ripe for once. Staff were the real highlight somehow; Marco at the front desk gave us hiking tips for Path of the Gods and even arranged a last-minute boat tour when we asked on a whim. Location is perfect, a short walk down to the beach and right near restaurants but quiet at night. Yes, it's pricey and parking in town is a nightmare, but that's Amalfi for you. Would absolutely return.

We stayed at the Hotel Ambassador for four nights in early October and honestly it exceeded what we expected for the price. Our room on the fifth floor was a good size, spotless, and the bed was genuinely comfortable, which matters a lot after long days of walking around. The front desk staff deserve a special mention: they gave us great restaurant recommendations, arranged a late checkout without any fuss, and even printed our boarding passes when the business center was busy. Breakfast was a highlight too, with fresh pastries, decent coffee, and eggs made to order. Location was excellent, a short walk to the metro and plenty of cafes nearby. Only tiny complaint was slow elevator service at peak times, but that's minor. Would absolutely return next trip.

We stayed three nights at the Conrad and honestly it exceeded expectations. The check-in was smooth, and we were upgraded to a partial ocean view room on the 28th floor, which made my wife's day. The bed was genuinely comfortable, blackout curtains worked perfectly, and the bathroom with the soaking tub was a nice touch after long days walking the city. Breakfast at the restaurant downstairs was excellent, though pricey, fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs, worth it once or twice. Housekeeping was prompt and they remembered we'd asked for extra pillows. Location is great too, easy walk to plenty of restaurants. Only tiny gripe: the lobby elevator wait at peak hours could be a bit long. Would absolutely return next trip.

We stayed at the Fairmont for three nights to celebrate our anniversary, and honestly it exceeded what we were hoping for. Check-in was smooth despite us arriving early, and they upgraded our room without us even asking, which was a lovely surprise. The room itself was spacious with a huge marble bathroom and a view of the city lights that we couldn't stop staring at. Housekeeping was attentive but never intrusive. We had breakfast downstairs twice, and the salmon eggs benedict was genuinely one of the best meals I've had in a while, though be warned it fills up fast after 9am. The concierge arranged dinner reservations for us and even remembered our anniversary when we returned that evening. Only tiny gripe was slow elevator waits during peak hours, but that's nitpicking. Would absolutely return.

We stayed here for four nights and honestly, it exceeded what I was expecting. The front desk staff, especially a guy named Marcus, went out of his way to make our check-in smooth even though we arrived way past midnight due to a delayed flight. Our room was clean, spacious, and the bed was genuinely comfortable -- I haven't slept that well in a hotel in ages. The music theme is everywhere, and even as someone who isn't a die-hard rock fan, I thought it was fun rather than cheesy. Breakfast had a solid spread of options and the coffee was actually good, which matters to me. The location was convenient for getting around, and the pool area was never too crowded. Minor nitpick: the elevator situation got a bit slow during peak times. Would definitely come back.

We stayed at the Hilton for a long weekend to celebrate our anniversary and honestly couldn't have asked for a better experience. Check-in was quick and the front desk agent even sent a small plate of chocolates up to our room when she learned the occasion, which was a genuinely thoughtful touch. The room itself was spacious, spotless, and had a surprisingly comfortable bed, a real highlight since hotel beds usually leave us sore. Housekeeping was consistent without being intrusive. The executive lounge breakfast had a nice spread, and the omelet station was excellent. Location was convenient, a short walk to plenty of restaurants. Only minor gripe: the pool got crowded Saturday afternoon. Overall, wonderful stay, friendly staff, and we'd absolutely return for our next trip. Highly recommend this property.

We stayed at the Homewood for three nights while visiting family and honestly it exceeded what I expected for the price. Check-in was quick and the front desk guy (Jamal, I think?) actually gave us a list of local places to eat instead of just handing us a map. The room was spacious with a proper kitchenette, which came in handy more than we thought it would. Bed was comfortable, AC worked well, and the free breakfast had real options, eggs, waffles, fresh fruit, not just sad pastries. One small note: the elevator was a bit slow during peak morning hours, but that's a minor gripe. The evening social on Wednesday with snacks was a nice touch we weren't expecting. Would definitely book here again if we're back in the area. Solid value and genuinely friendly staff.

We stayed at the Grand Hyatt for four nights over a long weekend and honestly can't find much to complain about. Check-in was quick, and the front desk agent actually took time to point out a few good restaurants nearby, which was a nice touch. Our room on the 14th floor was huge by city standards, with a super comfortable bed I kept 'testing' far too long each morning. Housekeeping was thorough without being intrusive. The breakfast buffet is worth it even if it feels a little pricey at first--fresh fruit, made-to-order omelets, and the coffee is decent. Pool and gym are clean and never crowded when we went. Only minor gripe is the elevator wait times during peak hours. Would book this place again without hesitation.

We stayed at the Intercontinental for our anniversary weekend and it honestly exceeded what we expected. Check-in was quick and the front desk agent noticed the occasion from our booking notes and sent up a plate of chocolates with a handwritten card, which was a lovely touch. Our room on a higher floor had a gorgeous view of the harbor, and the bed was probably the most comfortable I've slept in at any hotel, pillows included. Housekeeping was discreet and thorough, turndown service every evening. We used the concierge twice for dinner reservations and both spots were excellent. Breakfast buffet had a huge spread, though it does get busy around nine so go early. Only minor gripe was the wait for the elevator one morning, but that's hardly a complaint. Would absolutely return.

I stayed at the hotel james for three nights last month and honestly wasn't expecting much given the price, but it really exceeded my expectations. My room on the fourth floor was spacious, spotless, and the bed was genuinely comfortable--not one of those rock-hard hotel mattresses. The front desk staff, especially a woman named Priya, went out of her way to help me figure out public transit and even printed my boarding pass. Breakfast was included and while the selection wasn't huge, the coffee was good and the pastries were fresh. Location is a real strong point too: walking distance to several restaurants and maybe ten minutes from the main square. Only minor gripe was some noise from the street early in the morning, but nothing earplugs couldn't fix. Would absolutely come back.

We stayed at the Hotel Knickerbocker for a long weekend in the city and honestly it exceeded what I was expecting. The location near Times Square could have meant chaos, but the hotel itself feels like a quiet pocket of calm once you step inside. Our room was compact but thoughtfully designed, with a really comfortable bed and blackout curtains that made sleeping through the noise outside a non-issue. The bathroom had great water pressure and nice toiletries too. The staff were genuinely warm, not the fake-polite kind, and the concierge gave us two dinner recommendations that ended up being highlights of the trip. St. Cloud, the rooftop bar, is expensive but worth one drink for the view. Small knocks: elevators got busy at peak times and the AC ran a bit loud. Still, we'd absolutely return.

Truly enjoyed our three nights at the Monaco. The location is unbeatable, steps from everything but tucked away enough that the street noise never bothered us. Check-in was smooth, and the front desk staff went out of their way to recommend a couple of local restaurants that ended up being trip highlights. Our room was on the smaller side but beautifully designed, with a super comfortable bed, blackout curtains, and a rainfall shower that had great water pressure. Housekeeping kept everything immaculate, and they even left extra towels without us asking. The complimentary evening wine reception in the lobby was a nice surprise, a lovely way to unwind after a day of walking around. Minor quibble: the elevator is slow during peak morning hours, but honestly that's being picky. Would absolutely stay here again on our next visit.

Stayed at the Omni for three nights during a work conference and honestly had a lovely time. My room on the 14th floor was spacious, spotless, and the bed was genuinely comfortable--rare for a hotel, I usually struggle to sleep somewhere new. The staff went out of their way constantly; the concierge gave me excellent dinner recommendations downtown and the front desk fixed a keycard glitch within two minutes. Room service was a bit slow one night, but the food arrived hot and the carbonara was surprisingly good. Loved the lobby smell (I asked what scent it was, no shame). Checking out was quick and they stored my luggage after checkout without any fuss. Would absolutely stay here again next time I'm in town for business--maybe even bring the family for a weekend.

We stayed at the Hotel Palmer for three nights and honestly couldn't have asked for a better stay. The front desk staff went out of their way on arrival, offering us a room on a higher floor after I mentioned being a light sleeper, and it made a real difference. The bed was genuinely comfortable, and the shower had strong water pressure, which matters more to me than most hotel luxuries. Breakfast was simple but fresh--good coffee, pastries, and eggs that weren't sitting under a heat lamp forever. Location was a huge plus, walkable to the metro and a bunch of restaurants within a few blocks. Only tiny gripe: hallways could get a bit noisy around 10pm, but nothing earplugs wouldn't fix. Would happily book again next trip.

I stayed at the Sheraton for four nights for a work trip and honestly it exceeded my expectations. The front desk sorted out my early check-in without any fuss, which was great after a red-eye flight. My room on the 14th floor was spacious, spotless, and the bed--oh that bed, the Signature bedding thing they advertise is legit, I slept better than I do at home. Housekeeping was consistent every day, always restocking water and towels. The club lounge had a decent breakfast spread with fresh fruit and good coffee, though it got a bit crowded around 8:30. Location was perfect, walking distance to the metro and plenty of restaurants nearby. Only small gripe was the gym had a couple of broken machines, but there was plenty of equipment anyway. Staff overall were warm and genuinely helpful. Would absolutely stay here again.

I stayed at the Sofitel for three nights on a work trip and honestly couldn't fault it. The check-in was smooth, and the concierge went out of his way to book me a last-minute dinner reservation when everything nearby seemed full. My room on the eighth floor was spacious, spotless, and the bed was genuinely one of the most comfortable I've slept in at any hotel -- the pillows especially. Housekeeping respected my do-not-disturb mornings without issue. Breakfast had a great spread, the fresh pastries were worth getting up for, and the coffee was much better than the usual hotel machine stuff. The location is also super convenient, walking distance to the metro and plenty of restaurants. Only tiny gripe was a slight wait for the elevator at peak times, but that's minor. Would definitely return next trip.

We stayed at the Swissotel for four nights and honestly it exceeded what we expected. Check-in was quick and the front desk staff even remembered our names after the first day, which felt like a nice personal touch. Our room on a higher floor had an amazing view of the city skyline and was spotless when we arrived. The bed was genuinely comfortable -- my husband usually complains about hotel pillows but he slept great every night. Breakfast had a huge spread, everything from fresh fruit and pastries to made-to-order eggs, and the coffee was actually good, which is rare. Location was perfect too, walking distance to the main shopping street and a metro station right around the corner. Only tiny gripe was slow elevators at peak times, but that's minor. Would definitely come back.

We stayed at the Hotel Talbott for four nights and honestly, it exceeded what we expected. The location is fantastic, quiet side street but just a few blocks from the Magnificent Mile, so easy to walk everywhere without the chaos. Our room was spacious by city standards, and the bed was genuinely comfortable, which mattered because I usually sleep badly in hotels. What really won us over was the staff. The doorman remembered our names by day two, and when we asked the front desk for restaurant suggestions they gave us three spots we ended up loving, none of them touristy. The little touches, like fresh cookies in the afternoon and a real coffee maker in the room, felt thoughtful. Only tiny gripe was slow elevator on checkout day, but that's a minor thing. Would absolutely stay here again on our next Chicago trip.

I really wanted to like the Affinia, but our four nights there were a letdown from start to finish. The breakfast was a joke for the price of the room -- stale pastries, watery coffee, and by 8:30 the fruit bowl was empty and nobody bothered to refill it. The wifi was so unreliable that I gave up trying to work from the room and ended up camping out at a coffee shop down the street. Noise was a constant issue too; our room faced the street and we heard sirens, delivery trucks, and hallway conversations at all hours. The 'city view' advertised on the booking site turned out to be a stare directly into the neighboring building's wall of AC units. Staff were polite enough, but for this price I expected far more. Won't be returning.

We chose the Allegro based on the photos and the location, but the stay fell short of expectations almost immediately. Our room overlooked the alley, so the 'view' was a brick wall, dumpsters, and constant deliveries starting before 6 a.m. The bathroom was cramped and dated, with peeling wallpaper, a showerhead that barely had pressure, and a drain that seemed permanently slow. The room itself wasn't much better; there were stains on the carpet, smudges on the mirror, and what looked like old hair behind the nightstand, which made me question how thoroughly the housekeeping staff cleans between guests. As for the front desk, they were indifferent at best. When we mentioned the noise, we were told the hotel was full and given nothing in the way of an apology or adjustment. For the price, I expected far more and won't be returning.

I really wanted to love this place after reading the reviews, but our four nights felt like two weeks. The room itself was decent-sized, yet whoever cleaned it clearly rushed--crumbs under the desk, a sticky ring on the nightstand, and hair trailing one of the pillows. The bathroom was the real letdown: the shower head sputtered between scalding and lukewarm, the drain gurgled all night, and the grout had visible mildew along the tub edges. Staff interactions were cool at best. Front desk barely looked up during check-in, and when we asked for extra towels we waited nearly two hours. The concierge did help with a dinner reservation, I'll give him that. For what this costs, I expected thoroughness and warmth, and got neither. Won't be back.

I really wanted to love the Hotel Ambassador given everything I'd read beforehand, but our three-night stay left me underwhelmed, especially for what we paid. At nearly $300 a night, I expected more than a room where the carpet was worn at the edges and the light fixtures looked like they hadn't been updated since the nineties. The decor is trying hard for classic elegance but mostly reads as tired and dated, not timeless. Our window faced an air shaft and a brick wall rather than any kind of view, which was a real letdown considering I'd specifically requested something nicer. The front desk staff were around, but asking for an extra pillow felt like an inconvenience to them. Honestly, one night here would have been plenty--by night three I was ready to check out early. Disappointing overall.

I expected more from a property with the Conrad name, honestly. Our room looked fine at first glance, but a closer look told another story: crumbs behind the nightstand, stained upholstery on the chair, and something dry and sticky on the bathroom floor that never quite went away even after we asked housekeeping to redo it. The bathroom itself felt dated for this price bracket, with a shower that fluctuated wildly between lukewarm and scalding. We also underestimated how thin the walls were; every night we heard neighbors' TVs, hallway conversations, and the muffled bass from the bar downstairs until well past midnight. The staff weren't rude exactly, just indifferent. Nobody followed up on anything, requests took hours, and the concierge seemed annoyed to be asked basic questions. For nearly $400 a night, I can't recommend this place. won't return.

I wanted to love the Fairmont given its reputation, but our stay fell flat in nearly every way. We paid a premium for a 'city view' room, and what we got was mostly a glimpse of a rooftop ventilation system and an unobstructed look at the neighboring building's wall--maybe ten percent sky if we pressed our faces to the corner of the window. The neighbors weren't the problem, though; the hallway was. Housekeeping started their carts rattling past our door at 6:40 each morning, and the walls seemed to conduct every conversation next door. For this rate, I expected genuine care from the staff, but requests for extra towels took hours, and my question about late checkout was answered with a shrug and a flat 'that'll be a fee.' Dollars to donuts, this is not the luxury experience the price promises. We won't be back.

We'd been looking forward to staying at the Hard Rock for months, and honestly it fell flat in almost every way. Our room overlooked the loading dock, so instead of any kind of skyline we got dumpsters and delivery trucks rumbling in before dawn each morning. The bathroom was worse: tiny, with a shower that alternated between scalding and freezing, hair in the drain, and water pooling around the toilet because the seal was broken. Sleep was impossible anyway thanks to the thumping bass from the bar drifting up until 2 a.m. Then until nearly 1. The staff, save for one kind housekeeper, seemed genuinely annoyed by requests -- the front desk guy shrugged when I complained about the noise and offered nothing. For what they charge per night, this place is a rip-off. We won't be back.

I had high hopes for the Hilton given its reputation, but our three-night stay left us let down at nearly every turn. The 'city view' room we paid extra for mostly looked out onto a grey wall of office buildings and a rooftop of rattling AC units, so we kept the curtains drawn most of the time. Oddly, two nights felt like plenty -- not because we were worn out from sightseeing, but because there was little to enjoy in the room itself. The wifi was a real headache: it dropped constantly in the evenings and made even basic browsing frustrating. Staff interactions were hit or miss. One housekeeper was lovely, but the front desk seemed annoyed by questions, and an early-morning wakeup call we never requested jolted us awake at 5:30. For the price, I expected far more polish and warmth. I won't be rushing back.

I really expected more from this Homewood, especially at the rates they charge. The room itself was fine, but sleep was nearly impossible both nights. There's a highway right behind the property, and even with the window shut I could hear trucks rumbling past well after midnight. The HVAC unit also cycled loudly every twenty minutes like it was struggling. The wifi was the bigger frustration, though -- it dropped constantly and the 'premium' network I was apparently paying for in my rate barely loaded a Youtube video. When I called the front desk about it, I got a shrug and a suggestion to 'try standing closer to the door.' For nearly $180 a night, that's not acceptable. The breakfast was the one bright spot, but it doesn't make up for two rough nights. I won't be back.

Honestly, I expected a lot more from a Hyatt at this price point. We were there three nights and it felt like a week in the worst way. The room overlooked the loading dock, so every morning around 5:30 the delivery trucks started backing up with that relentless beeping. Even with earplugs I barely slept -- the walls are paper-thin too, and I could hear the neighbors' TV until well past midnight. When I called the front desk about the noise, they promised someone would look into it, and unsurprisingly nobody ever did. The view was a gray shaft between two buildings, nothing you'd want to linger on. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely. Two good things: the bed itself was comfortable, and the lobby coffee was decent. That's about all I can praise. Won't be returning.

I had high hopes for the InterContinental given the price, but our four nights felt like an eternity. The decor is badly in need of a refresh -- the lobby still has that heavy, dark 1990s look, and our room's floral bedspreads and scratched furniture only made it worse. The carpet in our room had visible stains near the closet, and I found a                		long hair in the bathroom on arrival, which honestly turned my stomach. Speaking of the bathroom, it was cramped, with a shower that alternated between scalding and freezing and a fan that rattled loudly the whole time. The front desk staff were polite but slow; it took nearly twenty minutes to get extra towels. For what this hotel charges, I expected far more. I won't be returning.

I really wanted to like this place, but the hotel james fell short in almost every way. The location is honestly the only bright spot -- it's walking distance to plenty of restaurants and shops, which made getting around easy. Unfortunately, that's where the positives end. Our room was not properly cleaned before check-in; there were crumbs on the desk and what looked like an old stain on the duvet. The bathroom was cramped and dated, with a shower that alternated between scalding and freezing no matter how carefully we adjusted the handle, and the Water dripped weakly the whole time. As for the staff, they seemed distracted and disinterested whenever we asked for anything, whether it was extra towels or a simple question about checkout. For the price we paid, I expected far more. Won't be returning.

We'd expected more from a property with this reputation. The room itself was fine at first glance, but sleep was impossible both nights thanks to the elevator bank directly through the wall--we heard the mechanical whine every few minutes until 2 a.m. Breakfast was the real letdown: $34 for a buffet where the eggs were rubbery, the fruit clearly came out of a can, and the coffee tasted burnt. Our bathroom had a persistent damp smell, and the shower drained so slowly I was standing in an inch of water by the end. The 'view' we paid a premium for? A mostly obstructed look at an air conditioning unit and a slice of roof. Staff were polite enough, but politeness doesn't fix a stay this pricey that delivered this little. Won't be returning.

I really wanted to love Hotel Monaco given the price, but our stay fell flat. The noise was the worst part -- our room faced the street, and between the bar downstairs and the streetcar clanging until well past midnight, sleep was nearly impossible even with earplugs. At nearly $400 a night, you'd expect soundproofing, decent towels, and a working thermostat; we got none of the above. The room also felt smaller than the photos suggested, and the 'luxury' wallpaper was peeling near the AC unit. Breakfast was a genuine letdown too: a cold buffet with watery eggs and stale pastries, not worth the $28 upcharge. Honestly, the two nights felt long rather than too short, and we checked out early on the last morning. For that kind of money, I expected far more. We won't be back.

I really wanted to love this place given the price, but our two nights at the Omni left us deflated. The room had promise, but the bathroom was the letdown: the shower alternated between scalding and cold, the drain barely kept up, and there was grout mildew in the corners that no amount of good towels could distract from. Our 'city view' looked straight into the neighboring office tower, so we kept the curtains drawn the whole time. The wifi kept dropping every few minutes, which was maddening since I had a work call to take -- I ended up using hotspot data from my phone. Honestly, one night would have been plenty; by the second morning we were eager to leave. The front desk staff were pleasant, to be fair, but pleasant staff can't fix a bathroom and a bandwidth problem. Not again.

Honestly expected more from Hotel Palmer given the rate they charge. The one bright spot is the location, which is genuinely convenient, steps from the metro and walking distance to several restaurants. Unfortunately, that's where the good news ends. My room, while not dirty, clearly hadn't been deep cleaned in a while -- dust on the lampshade and a sticky film on the bedside table. The bathroom was the real letdown: a cramped shower with weak water pressure and grout that looked like it hadn't seen a scrub brush all year. For what I paid, I'd expect fresh towels without chasing housekeeping and working lights above the mirror. Between the thin walls and the street noise at 5 a.m., sleep was a struggle. Decent neighborhood, but I don't think I got my money's worth here.

Honestly, this stay was a letdown for what we paid. The Sheraton charges premium rates but the wifi in our room barely worked, dropping every few minutes and making it impossible to get any work done, which was the whole reason we booked. When I mentioned it at the front desk, the staff member just shrugged and said 'it happens sometimes' without offering any fix or even an apology. Housekeeping skipped our room entirely one afternoon and we had to call twice to get fresh towels. For over $300 a night, I expected far better service and a connection that actually functioned. The room itself was clean enough, though dated and smaller than the photos suggested. By the last day we were genuinely ready to leave, and the four nights felt much longer than they should have. Won't be returning.

We paid Sofitel prices expecting a proper luxury stay and left genuinely let down. The first night was a write-off: the room overlooked the mechanical units on the roof, and even with the windows sealed the droning kept me up until nearly three. When I asked to move, the second room was better for noise but the air conditioning rattled constantly, so sleep was a struggle either way. Housekeeping was hit and miss too -- a makeup-stained hand towel stayed in the bathroom our whole stay, and one afternoon the bed wasn't made at all. The decor hasn't been refreshed in years, honestly; the purple-and-gold accent scheme and scuffed armchair felt very early 2000s, nothing like the sleek lobby photos online. Staff were polite enough, but politeness doesn't fix a worn-out, noisy hotel. I won't be back.

I expected far more from a property carrying the Swissotel name. We arrived for a three-night stay and were put in a room facing the service alley, so the 'city view' I'd requested never materialized -- just bins, deliveries and a brick wall. It was also noisier than I'd imagined: constant beeping from trucks in the morning and hallway chatter late at night despite the do-not-disturb sign. The bathroom was the real letdown. Water pressure barely trickled, the shower temperature swung from cold to scalding, and the grout in the corners was stained with mildew. The decor felt frozen around 2009, with a faded brown carpet, scratched cabinetry and that beige-on-beige look that just reads tired now. Staff were polite when we flagged issues, but nothing much changed. For the price, I won't be returning.

I had high hopes for the Talbott given its reputation and the rates they charge, but my four-night stay fell flat in nearly every way. The walls are paper thin--I could hear my neighbors' conversations and the elevator clanking until well past midnight, so I barely slept more than a few hours each night. The staff seemed*o perform a strange kind of politeness that never felt genuine; my requests for extra towels took two phone calls and several hours. For nearly $400 a night, I expected far better. Honestly, three nights in would have been plenty--I was counting the days until checkout, which is never a good sign. The location is convenient, I'll grant that, but convenience doesn't justify an underwhelming, overpriced experience. I won't be returning and can't recommend it.

We stayed at the Affinia for four nights and honestly couldn't wait to check out. The room faced the street, and the noise was relentless -- garbage trucks at 5am, sirens throughout the night, and thin walls that let us hear every conversation in the hallway. Sleep was basically impossible without earplugs, which we didn't have the first two nights. The wifi was another letdown; it dropped constantly and was so slow in the evenings that streaming anything was a gamble. For the price, I expected far better. The staff were pleasant enough, but that doesn't make up for exhaustion every morning. By the last day, the stay felt way too long, even though friends had told us it would fly by. Disappointing overall, and we won't be returning.

I had high hopes coming here, but Hotel Allegro really let me down. The bathroom was cramped and clearly overdue for a renovation--mildew in the shower grout, a sink that drained painfully slowly, and a wobbly toilet seat that made everything feel grimy. The staff barely acknowledged us; check-in felt like an inconvenience to them, and when I asked a question at the desk, I got a shrug instead of an answer. Noise was the worst part: the walls are paper-thin, and I heard doors slamming and conversations well past midnight. My sleep suffered badly both nights, waking up4 almost hourly. By the time we left, we were exhausted and relieved to go. For the price, it wasn't remotely worth it, and I won't be returning.

We had high hopes for Hotel Amalfi given the price, but honestly it felt overpriced for what you get. The room was technically clean, the sheets looked fresh and the bathroom had no grime, but there was a persistent musty smell near the window that no amount of airing out seemed to fix. Noise was the real dealbreaker for us: the walls are paper thin, and we heard every conversation in the hallway plus what I swear was a vacuum at six each morning. The decor also feels stuck decades ago, with worn carpet, dated furniture, and lighting from another era. For what they charge per night, I expected something far more polished and restful. Staff were polite enough, but I probably wouldn't return or recommend it to friends.

I really wanted to like this hotel, but between the price we paid and what we got, it fell short. The location is honestly its best feature, just a few minutes' walk from the metro and plenty of restaurants, but that's about where the good news ends. Our room faced the street and the noise was relentless until well past midnight, with doors slamming in the corridor all night too. The wifi barely worked in the room; it kept dropping every few minutes, which was a real problem since I needed to join a couple of video calls during my stay. At over 200 euros a night, I expect reliable internet and some soundproofing, not earplugs and hotspoting from my phone. The staff were polite enough, but politeness doesn't fix a room that feels overpriced. I won't be returning.

I really wanted to love the Conrad given its reputation, but our stay was a letdown. At nearly $500 a night, I expected far more than what we got. The room looked fine at first glance, but on closer inspection there were coffee stains on the desk, hairs in the bathroom, and a dusty vent. Housekeeping barely refreshed anything during our three nights. Wifi was spotty at best -- it dropped constantly, which made working from the room frustrating. Breakfast was the biggest disappointment: the buffet looked tired, eggs were lukewarm, fruit was soggy, and one morning we waited almost twenty minutes for coffee before giving up. The location is convenient and the lobby is impressive, but honestly the service and details don't justify the price. I'd stay elsewhere next time.

We stayed at the Fairmont for four nights, and by the second morning I was honestly counting down until checkout. The room itself looked impressive at first glance, but the wow factor faded fast. Sleep quality was terrible throughout our stay -- thin walls meant we heard every slammed door in the corridor, and the air conditioning rattled loudly all night no matter what setting we used. I woke up exhausted every single day. Breakfast was the biggest letdown: for the prices they charge, I expected fresh and abundant, but the buffet was lukewarm, the eggs rubbery, and the coffee tasted like it had been sitting for hours. When we mentioned this at the front desk, we got a polite shrug and nothing more. For this kind of money, the value simply isn't there. We won't be back.

We honestly expected more from a place with such a big name. The moment we walked in, the decor felt dated -- the so-called rock memorabilia looked tired, the carpets were stained, and everything had a worn 2005 vibe that no amount of neon could hide. Our room was no better: scuffed furniture, a wobbly bed frame, and a bathroom that smelled vaguely of mildew. The shower dripped constantly, the grout was black in places, and the towels were thin and gray. The staff didn't help much either; check-in took forever, and when we asked for extra pillows, the front desk seemed annoyed rather than accommodating. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely. Honestly, two nights here already felt too long. We won't be back, and we'd think twice before recommending it to anyone.

We stayed four nights at this Hilton and honestly couldn't wait to leave. The photos online showed a beautiful city view, but our window faced directly at the neighbouring office building, so we kept the curtains drawn most of the time. The room itself showed its age: stains on the carpet, dust on the bedside lamps, and hair in the bathroom that clearly hadn't been cleaned before our arrival. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely. The staff were polite enough at check-in, but every request afterwards felt like an inconvenience; it took three calls and nearly two hours to get extra towels. Even the breakfast staff barely acknowledged us. Four nights felt far too long in a place like this, and at these prices we expected much better. We won't be returning.

I really wanted to like this Homewood Suites, and the location is honestly its one saving grace -- right off the highway with quick access to restaurants and the business park, which made my morning commute painless. Unfortunately, everything else fell flat. Despite paying for an upper-floor room, I faced a parking lot and a strip mall, so the 'view' was a joke. Worse, the walls are paper-thin; I heard my neighbor's TV until midnight and doors slamming at 6 a.m. both nights. The breakfast, usually the highlight of this chain, was a letdown: cold eggs, watery oatmeal, and the waffle iron ran out of mix both mornings with no staff restocking. The front desk did offer points as compensation, but between the noise and the sad hot plate, I won't be returning.

I expected more from a Hyatt, honestly. The room itself was okay at first glance, but the bathroom was grimy around the tub edges, the showerhead sputtered inconsistently, and there was a persistent damp smell no amount of venting seemed to fix. Sleep quality was poor both nights -- thin walls meant hallway conversations and door slams came through clearly, and the AC unit rattled loudly every time it kicked on. To be fair, the location is genuinely convenient: right by the metro stop, plenty of restaurants within a five-minute walk, and easy airport access. But convenience alone doesn't justify the price. At nearly $300 a night, dealing with a musty bathroom and two rough nights of sleep felt like a bad deal. I won't be rushing back.

I had really high hopes for the InterContinental given its reputation, but my three-night stay left me honestly underwhelmed. The location is undeniably convenient, right in the heart of everything and steps from the metro, so I'll give it that. Unfortunately, that central position meant constant traffic noise filtering into my room even on the fourteenth floor, andInforma I barely slept. Housekeeping also seemed to miss my room one day entirely -- used glasses sat out until evening, and I found hairs on the bathroom floor on arrival. The front desk staff were polite enough but slow to resolve anything; requesting a room change took two phone calls and a visit in person. For the price point, the service and upkeep simply don't match. I expected far more from a property calling itself a luxury hotel.

I had really hoped for better from the Hotel James, but our stay fell short in almost every way. The bathroom was the biggest letdown -- the shower barely maintained lukewarm pressure, the grout was black with mildew, and the fan rattled loud enough to wake the whole room. Sleep wasn't much better, honestly. The mattress sagged in the middle and street noise poured through a window that refused to seal, so we tossed and turned both nights. Cleanliness was questionable too: sticky rings on the nightstand, a gym towel someone left under the bed, and dust along every skirting board. Honestly, even one more night would have felt too long. The front desk staff was pleasant, but that alone can't rescue a stay this disappointing. We won't be back.

I really wanted to love the Knickerbocker given its reputation, but our stay fell flat. The noise was relentless -- our room faced the street and the bar below kept us up past 2am both nights, with doors slamming in the hallway constantly. The wifi was spotty at best; it dropped every time I tried to join a video call, which was the whole reason I booked. The bathroom looked sleek in photos but in reality the shower tolled lukewarm and the drain gurgled ominously. As for the view, we paid extra for a 'city view' and got a wall of scaffolding with a sliver of brick. Staff were polite enough, but for this price I expected far more. Disappointing.

We had high hopes for the Monaco based on the photos, but our stay was honestly a letdown. Breakfast was the biggest disappointment: the eggs were cold, the pastries tasted like they'd been sitting out since the previous evening, and they ran out of coffee twice while we waited. The staff seemed indifferent at best--we asked for extra towels at the front desk and got a shrug and a fifteen-minute wait with no apology. As for sleep, forget about it. Our room faced the street and the noise from traffic and late-night revelers went on until nearly 3 a.m., plus the walls are so thin we could hear our neighbor's TV. The bed was decent, but that hardly mattered when we were waking up every couple of hours. For this price, I expected far better.

We stayed at the Omni for a long weekend and honestly expected more for the price. The WiFi was practically unusable, dropping every few minutes, which made it impossible to get any work done. Our room overlooked the parking garage and a stretch of rooftops with AC units humming away, so there was nothing pleasant to look at. Sleep was a struggle too: the walls are thin, we heard hallway conversations and elevator dings well past midnight, and the mattress sagged in the middle. The staff didn't help matters. Front desk agents seemed annoyed whenever we asked for anything, and a request for extra towels took nearly four hours to arrive. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely. Convenient location, but between the noise, the weak connection, and the indifferent service, we won't be returning.

I really wanted to like Hotel Palmer, but this stay was a letdown from start to finish. The bathroom had mold creeping along the grout lines, and the shower drain backed up on our second morning, leaving standing water with nowhere to go. We'd booked a room with a view we were promised would be scenic -- instead we stared directly at a grimy brick wall and the kitchen's ventilation ducts, humming day and night. The noise wandered in from the street until nearly 2 a.m., plus hallway conversations echoed like the walls were paper. As for the staff, they barely acknowledged us; the front desk guy was glued to his phone and gave a shrug when we mentioned the drain. For these prices, I expected basic competence. Won't be back.

We stayed at the Sheraton for three nights and left genuinely disappointed. The photos online promised a lovely outlook, but our 'view' was mostly a grey parking garage wall with a slice of rooftop AC units humming away. Breakfast was the biggest letdown: the scrambled eggs were lukewarm and watery, the fruit looked tired from the day before, and the coffee was so weak we ended up paying extra at a cafe across the street. Sleep was a struggle too. Even though our room was far from the elevator, the hallway noise carried badly, and every night around 11pm we could hear music and laughter from the bar two floors down until well past midnight. The bed itself was decent, but that hardly matters when the walls are this thin. For the price, we expected far better.

I had high hopes for this Sofitel given the price, but our stay was sadly underwhelming. The bathroom was the biggest letdown -- the shower drained so slowly that water pooled around our feet, and there was visible mold along the grout near the tub. Housekeeping came late most days, too. On the plus side, the location is genuinely convenient, just a short walk from the metro and plenty of restaurants, so getting around was easy. Our room faced a narrow back alley, so instead of city views we stared at air conditioners and brick walls the whole week. Breakfast repeated the pattern of disappointment: cold eggs, watery coffee, and a buffet that never got restocked on time despite the hefty price. For a property with this reputation, I expected far more attention to detail. Won't be returning.

I really expected more from a hotel with this reputation. The room itself was decent, but the noise was relentless -- I could hear the elevator shaft all night, plus doors slamming in the hallway until well past midnight. I'd booked four nights and honestly by night two I was counting down. The staff were polite enough at check-in, but every request afterward seemed to be someone else's job; housekeeping was never called back and my wake-up call never came on the last morning. For nearly 300 euros a night, this felt poor value -- I've stayed in far cheaper places that delivered more comfort and actual service. The location is convenient, I'll grant that. But overall a disappointing, restless stay that I wouldn't repeat at these prices.

I had hopes for the Talbott based on its reputation, but our three-night stay was a letdown from start to finish. The wifi barely functioned -- it dropped constantly in the evenings and took ages to load anything, which made working from the room impossible. Staff ranged from indifferent to outright curt; when we mentioned the thermostat wasn't working, nobody ever came to check it. Breakfast was the biggest disappointment: cold eggs, lukewarm coffee, and a sad pastry selection that looked like it had been sitting out since the day before. The rooms themselves are part of the problem, too -- the decor feels straight out of the early 2000s, with worn carpet, scuffed furniture, and heavy drapes that didn't quite close. For the price point, I expected far more. We won't be back.

I really wanted to like this place, but the Affinia let me down at nearly every turn. Check-in took over twenty minutes while the front desk clerk fumbled with the computer, and nobody offered an apology. My room looked tired, with a stained armchair and an AC unit that rattled all night no matter what I did. The 'suite' bathroom had a slow drain that left the sink filling up every morning. Housekeeping skipped my room entirely one day and left only two towels the next.(Location is fine, I'll give them that, but at these prices I expected far more.) When I mentioned the noise at checkout, the response was a shrug. Skip this one and book elsewhere.

We booked Hotel Allegro for a long weekend and honestly I can't figure out how it has the rating it does. First off, we arrived at 3pm, close to check-in, but the room wasn't ready until nearly 5. No apology, just 'come back later.' When we finally got in, the air conditioning was barely working and the room overlooked the alley, so we got delivery trucks beeping at 5am both mornings. The elevator situation is a disaster too -- two elevators for the whole building means long waits every single time. Breakfast at the restaurant downstairs cost way more than it should for cold eggs and slow service. Ask the front desk a simple question and you get a shrug._LOCATION_ I wanted to like this place, the lobby is pretty, but pretty doesn't make up for everything else. We won't be back.

I really wanted to love this place given the price, but our four nights here were a letdown. The AC in our room never cooled properly no matter what we set it to, and after sweating through two nights they finally moved us, only for the new room to smell faintly like mildew. Breakfast was included and pushing it -- diluted juice, lukewarm eggs, and the coffee machine ran empty most mornings. The pool was closed 'for maintenance' our entire stay, which nobody mentioned at booking. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely and knocked at 8:30am the next. Location is fine, walkable to the beach, and the front desk clerk on Tuesday was genuinely kind. But for what we paid, we expected far better. Probably won't be back.

I really wanted to like the Ambassador, but our stay was a letdown from start to finish. Check-in took nearly half an hour because the front desk was staffed by one visibly overwhelmed clerk. The room itself was dated, with a sagging mattress, a wobbly desk chair, and an air conditioning unit that rattled loudly every time it kicked on. We asked three times about the AC before anyone came up, and even then the fix lasted a day. Housekeeping skipped our floor one afternoon entirely. The location is decent, I'll grant that, and the morning coffee in the lobby was fine, but for this price I expected far more. The hallways smelled musty, and our window faced a brick wall. We won't be returning.

I had high hopes for the Conrad given the price point, but this stay left me genuinely frustrated. Check-in took nearly forty minutes because apparently they couldn't find my reservation, and nobody offered an apology so much as a shrug. The room itself looked nice at first glance, but the air conditioning rattled all night and the shower went lukewarm by day two. Housekeeping skipped our floor entirely one afternoon and we had to call twice to get fresh towels. The concierge recommended a restaurant that turned out to be closed for renovations, which tells you how current their information is. For a hotel charging this much, the service felt careless at every turn. The location is convenient, I'll give it that, but I won't be returning and can't recommend it to anyone expecting the luxury experience they advertise.

I really expected more from the Fairmont, honestly. We paid for a room with a view and got one mostly facing another building, plus the air conditioning rattled so loudly the first night that I barely slept. Called the front desk twice and someone said they'd send engineering up, but nobody ever showed. The room itself felt tired, worn carpet edges, a bathroom door that wouldn't close properly, and housekeeping skipped our room entirely one day. I will say the lobby is beautiful and the doormen were lovely, but the actual guest experience didn't match the price tag at all. Breakfast in the restaurant ran us nearly $90 for two people and the eggs were cold. For what this hotel charges, the attention to detail just isn't there. Not sure we'd come back.

I really wanted to love the Hard Rock, especially after paying what I did, but the whole stay felt like a letdown. Check-in took almost half an hour because they were short-staffed, and nobody apologized even once. The room itself looked tired -- scuffed walls, a lamp that didn't work, and the AC rattled all night no matter what I set it to. I called the front desk twice about it and got a different answer each time, and maintenance never actually showed up. The 'rock and roll' theme is everywhere, but it mostly means loud music blasting in the lobby at 11pm right outside the rooms. Breakfast was overpriced for what it was, and the coffee tasted like it had been sitting for hours. Honestly the location was the only saving grace. I won't be back.

I really expected more from a Hilton, honestly. We arrived around 3pm and our room still wasn't ready, then we stood waiting another 40 minutes with no apology or explanation. When we finally got in, the carpet had stains near the window and the AC unit rattled all night, so sleep was basically out of the question. The front desk staff varied wildly -- one woman was pleasant, but the guy on the night shift acted like asking for extra towels was a huge inconvenience. Breakfast cost $28 per person and the eggs were rubbery, the coffee barely lukewarm. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely and I had to call twice to get it sorted. The location is convenient, I'll give it that, but for nearly $300 a night I couldn't wait to check out. Won't be rushing back.

Honestly really disappointed with my stay at the Homewood. The ads make it look like a cozy extended-stay spot but the reality is way off. My first room had a stained couch and the AC rattled all night, so I barely slept. They moved me the next day, which was fine, but the new room's kitchenette was missing half the dishes and the dishwasher smelled weird. Housekeeping skipped my room twice despite my requests. The breakfast was the one bright spot the first morning, but by day three the eggs were cold and half the trays were empty with no staff around to restock. The location is okay, nothing special. For the price I expected a lot more. I won't be back and can't really recommend this place to anyone.

I had such high hopes for this Hyatt based on the price, but honestly the stay fell flat in almost every way. Check-in took nearly half an hour because apparently they were short-staffed, and nobody apologized or even acknowledged the wait. My room overlooked the loading dock, so I was woken up at 5:30 every morning by beeping trucks. The air conditioning rattled so loudly I had to shut it off the second night and just sweat it out. Housekeeping skipped my floor one day entirely, and when I called the front desk about fresh towels, they never came. The breakfast buffet was soggy and lukewarm both mornings, not at all what you'd expect at these rates. The location was fine, I'll give it that, but that's about the only thing going for it. I won't be returning, even though I usually stay loyal to this brand.

Honestly, I expected way more from a hotel with this name on it. Check-in took almost forty minutes because they'd somehow lost my reservation, and by the time I got to my room around 6pm, the tech I'd requested still wasn't set up. The room itself looked tired--scuffed baseboards, a stained armchair in the corner, and the air conditioning rattled all night no matter what I did with the thermostat. Housekeeping skipped my room entirely on the second day even after I called twice about it. Breakfast was the real letdown though: cold eggs, no decaf available, and a hostess who seemed annoyed anyone showed up before 8. The location is genuinely convenient, which is the only nice thing I can say. For nearly $400 a night, this was a disappointing stay and I won't be returning.

I had really high hopes for the James based on the photos, but my stay last weekend fell flat in almost every way. The room looked chic in the pictures online, but in person it felt dated and the air conditioning rattled all night, keeping me up until I finally gave up around 3am and called the desk. They offered to move me to another floor, but the new room had the same problem. The shower took forever to get hot, and when it did, the water pressure was pathetic. Housekeeping knocked on my door at 8am both mornings even though I asked for late service. The front desk staff seemed annoyed every time I asked for anything, including a simple extra pillow that took four hours to arrive. The location is fine, but honestly that's the only thing going for this place. At this price point I expected far better. Won't be back.

Honestly expected more from a hotel at this price point. Checked in around 4pm and my room still wasn't ready, then when I finally got in around 5:30 the AC was barely working. Front desk offered to 'look into it' but it never really cooled down during my whole three-night stay. The room itself was decently designed but small, and you could hear the elevator whirring all night through the wall. Housekeeping skipped my floor entirely one day, and when I called down I got transferred twice before anyone picked up. The bar downstairs is gorgeous, I'll give them that, but service there was slow even when it was half empty. Location is fine, near the theater district, but for this money I'd rather stay a few blocks away and actually sleep well. Won't be back.

I really wanted to like this place, but our stay at the Hotel Monaco fell flat on almost every count. Check-in took nearly half an hour because they claimed they couldn't find our reservation, even though I had the confirmation email right on my phone. The room itself was smaller than the photos suggested, and the air conditioning rattled all night like it was about to give up. Housekeeping skipped our room completely one day, and when we called the front desk about it, we got a shrug and a promise that never materialized. The location is decent and the lobby is pretty, sure, but that doesn't make up for lukewarm breakfast, hallway noise, and the overall sense that the money we spent went straight into the interior design rather than the service. Won't be back.

Honestly I expected more from the Omni. We paid a premium rate for a room that turned out to be noticeably tired--scuffed walls, a bathroom fan that rattled all night, and a TV remote with dead batteries that nobody seemed bothered to replace. Check-in took nearly half an hour because the front desk was understaffed on a Friday evening, and nobody apologized for it. Housekeeping skipped our room entirely one day, and when I called down about it, I got a shrug in the form of 'we'll get to it tomorrow.' The location is admittedly convenient, but for this price the walls were thin enough that I heard every hallway conversation at 6am. The gym was decent, sure, but that's not enough. Won't be back.

I had high hopes for the Palmer given its history and location, but my stay last weekend was a letdown from start to finish. Check-in took nearly 45 minutes because they claimed my reservation had 'disappeared' from the system, even though I had a confirmation email right there on my phone. When I finally got to my room, the air conditioning barely worked and the room felt stuffy and dated -- worn carpet, a bathroom with a sink that drained painfully slowly, and hair in the tub when I arrived. I called the front desk twice about maintenance and no one ever came up. Breakfast in the lobby restaurant was another low point; cold eggs and a 20-minute wait for coffee. The location honestly saved this from being a total disaster, but at these prices I expected far more. Won't be back.

I really wanted to like the Sheraton, but the stay fell short in too many ways. The room smelled faintly of smoke despite being a non-smoking floor, and the carpet looked like it hadn't been replaced in years. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely, and when I called the front desk twice about it, nobody followed up. The elevator wait times were brutal in the mornings, sometimes ten minutes, with conference crowds crammed in. Breakfast at the restaurant cost $28 per person and both the food and service were mediocre at best. On the plus side, the location is convenient and the bed itself was reasonably comfortable. Still, for a hotel charging these rates, I expect far better attention to basics. I won't be returning.

Honestly expected much more from a Sofitel. Check-in took forever because the front desk seemed staffed by one overwhelmed employee, and when I finally got to my room the air conditioning barely worked. I called down twice about it and someone said maintenance would come up, but nobody ever showed. The room itself felt tired -- scuffed furniture, a carpet with visible stains near the window, and the 'luxury' bedding was just average at best. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely and we had to request towels ourselves. Breakfast was the final letdown: cold eggs, slow service, and an absurd price for what it was. Location is decent, I'll grant that, and the doorman was genuinely kind. But for these rates? Applies nowhere near the standard. Won't be returning.

I had high hopes for the Swissotel given its reputation, but my stay last week was honestly a letdown. Check-in took nearly forty minutes because apparently they were short-staffed, and nobody apologized or offered anything for the wait. My room had a decent view but the air conditioning rattled all night and freezing water came out of the 'hot' tap every morning. Housekeeping skipped my room entirely one day, and when I called the front desk about it they said someone would come by, which never happened. The gym equipment looked tired and half the treadmills were out of order. Breakfast in the restaurant was overpriced for what you got, and service there was slow even though it wasn't crowded. For the money, I expected far better. Probably won't be back.

We stayed at the Talbott in January and honestly left disappointed. The lobby and location are nice, I'll give them that, but the room we got felt tired and worn. Scratches on the furniture, a bathroom fan that rattled all night, and the heater could not keep up -- we woke up freezing twice. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely and we had to call down to get towels. The front desk staff were polite but slow; checking in took almost twenty minutes even though there was no line. Parking valet took forty minutes to bring our car when we checked out. For the price, I expected much better comfort and service. There are plenty of other options in the Gold Coast, and next time we'll try one of them. Probably won't be back.

I really wanted to like this place, but our stay at the Affinia was disappointing from start to finish. Check-in took forever because the front desk was understaffed, and when we finally got to our room, it smelled vaguely of smoke despite being non-smoking. The AC unit rattled all night, so neither of us slept well. Housekeeping missed our room entirely one day, and when I called down about it, they promised fresh towels that never showed up. The location is decent, I'll give them that, but for the price we paid I expected much better. Breakfast was cold and the coffee was terrible. The front desk clerk did comp us a parking night, which was nice, but overall I can't recommend this hotel. We won't be returning.

We stayed at Hotel Allegro for three nights and honestly left pretty disappointed. Check-in took nearly forty minutes because only one person was at the desk. Our room overlooked the street and the noise went on until 2am every night - bring earplugs. The air conditioning barely worked, and when we reported it, someone came, jiggled something, and left. Breakfast was the real letdown: thin selection, lukewarm eggs, and coffee from a machine that tasted burnt. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely. The location is genuinely convenient, which is why I'm giving two stars instead of one, but for this price I expected much better. We won't be returning, and I'd suggest looking elsewhere if comfort matters to you.

We had such high hopes for Hotel Amalfi, but honestly the whole stay fell flat. The room was nowhere near as nice as the photos online -- worn carpet, a bathroom door that wouldn't close properly, and the air conditioning barely worked even after we reported it twice. Staff were polite enough but slow to fix anything, and housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely. Breakfast was the real letdown: stale bread, watery coffee, and the same sparse spread every single morning. The location is decent, sure, but you can hear street noise all night through thin windows, which made sleeping miserable. For the price we paid, I expected far more. Definitely won't be returning and can't really recommend this place unless you're just desperate for a bed.

Honestly one of the most disappointing stays I've had in a while. The photos online make the lobby look glamourous, but the reality is tired carpets, flickering corridor lights, and an air conditioning unit in my room that rattled all night. I called the front desk twice about it and both times someone promised maintenance would come up; nobody ever did. The bathroom had a weird smell I couldn't place, and the shower went from hot to freezing without warning. Breakfast was the final insult -- cold eggs, weak coffee, and a staff member who cleared my table before I was finished with it. For what they charge per night, you expect at least basic competence. Location is convenient, sure, but that's the only good thing I can say. I won't be back and can't recommend it to anyone.

We stayed at the Conrad for our anniversary and honestly left feeling let down. The lobby is gorgeous, no argument there, but that's where the good impressions ended. Check-in took nearly 40 minutes even though we'd booked weeks in advance. Our room had a musty smell and the AC rattled all night. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely and never came back after we called. Breakfast was chaotic both mornings -- waiting 25 minutes for coffee, cold eggs, staff who seemed overwhelmed. For a hotel that charges this much, the service simply didn't match the price tag. The executive lounge ran out of food before 8pm. Would not stay here again, especially not for a special occasion. Plenty of other options in the area that deliver better.

I had such high hopes for the Fairmont given its reputation, but our stay last week was a real letdown. Check-in took nearly forty minutes because apparently they were short-staffed, and no one apologized. The room itself was worn out - stains on the carpet, a bathroom door that wouldn't close properly, and the air conditioning rattled all night. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely, and when we called about it, they brought towels hours later but never actually cleaned. Room service arrived cold twice, and the breakfast buffet was overpriced for what it offered. The concierge gave us wrong directions twice, sending us across town unnecessarily. For a hotel at this price point, staff should be attentive and the rooms spotless. Honestly, it felt like a three-star property charging five-star rates. We won't be back.

We were so excited to stay here for my husband's birthday weekend, but honestly the whole thing was a letdown from start to finish. Check-in took nearly an hour because the line barely moved and there were only two people working. Our room had a broken AC that blew warm air the entire first night, and when we called the front desk they said someone would come up but nobody ever did. The 'rock star' atmosphere they advertise just feels like a garish gift shop attached to a mediocre hotel. Pool was packed with kids until closing and getting a lounge chair was basically impossible. Breakfast at the cafe cost almost $60 for two people and the food was lukewarm at best. Location-wise it's far from the beach unless you drive. For the price we paid, I expected so much more. We won't be back.

I really expected more from a Hilton, honestly. The lobby looks impressive when you walk in, but that's where the good impression ends. Check-in took almost forty minutes because their system was down and nobody seemed to know how to handle it manually. My room wasn't ready until nearly 4pm despite a confirmed early check-in request. The room itself felt tired -- stained carpet, a bathroom door that wouldn't stay closed, and the AC rattled all night so I barely slept. Housekeeping skipped my floor entirely one day and when I called down, no one came. Breakfast was the biggest letdown: lukewarm eggs, ran out of coffee twice, and a fifteen-minute wait for a table even though half the restaurant was empty. Staff tried to be polite but everything felt disorganized and understaffed. For the price, I'd book elsewhere next time.

We stayed here three nights for a family visit and honestly expected better from Homewood. The first room they put us in smelled strongly of cigarette smoke even though it's supposed to be non-smoking, and it took over an hour to get moved. The new room was okay but the AC unit rattled all night and the pull-out sofa bed had stains on the mattress. Breakfast was a letdown too--eggs were watery, some items ran out and weren't replaced, and the seating area was always a mess. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely and we had to ask for towels at the front desk. The location is convenient, I'll give it that, and a couple of staff members were friendly, but for the price I can't recommend it. We won't be back.

I really expected more from a Hyatt, honestly. Checked in around 4pm only to wait nearly 40 minutes because they were 'short on housekeeping staff,' and the room I finally got still smelled faintly of cigarettes despite being labeled non-smoking. The AC rattled all night like it was about to take off, so I barely slept. Bathroom had hair on the floor when I arrived, and the shower took a solid five minutes to get warm. Breakfast was a disappointment too -- cold eggs, coffee machine empty for over half an hour with nobody refilling it. Front desk staff were polite enough, but that doesn't make up for a $300-plus night that felt more like a budget motel. I won't be rushing back to this location anytime soon.

I really wanted to love this hotel given the price, but the Intercontinental fell short in ways I didn't expect. Check-in took nearly 40 minutes because apparently they were short-staffed, and no one apologized. My room had a musty smell that never fully went away, even after I called housekeeping twice. The air conditioning rattled all night, which made sleeping miserable before an important meeting. Breakfast was the biggest letdown--cold eggs, a shortage of coffee cups, and a line out the door with only two staff working. The concierge gave us wrong directions twice. For a property branding itself as luxury, the service felt more like a budget chain. The location is decent and the lobby is beautiful, but that's where the good ends. Probably won't be back.

We stayed at the Hotel James for three nights and honestly can't figure out how it gets such decent ratings. Check-in took forever because apparently only one person works the desk in the evenings, and when we finally got to our room the AC was barely blowing cool air. Asked twice about it before anyone came up. The hallway carpets were stained and the whole place just felt tired. Breakfast was the biggest letdown, lukewarm eggs, ran out of coffee both mornings, and no one refilled anything. Our window overlooked the loading dock, so we were woken at 5:45am bydeliveries every day. Bathroom had a musty smell that never really went away. Staff were polite enough but completely ineffective. For the price, there are far better options nearby. Won't be returning.

We stayed at the Knickerbocker for a long weekend and honestly expected much more for the price. Check-in took nearly forty minutes because they were 'short-staffed,' and the room wasn't ready until after 4pm even though we arrived at 2. The room itself was small and the street noise was relentless -- garbage trucks, sirens, everything -- despite requesting a quiet floor. Housekeeping skipped us entirely one day and we had to call twice for fresh towels. The rooftop bar looked appealing in photos but was so packed and overpriced ($22 for a mediocre cocktail) that we gave up after one round. Breakfast at the restaurant cost a fortune for cold eggs. Location is truly great, near Times Square but that's about the only upside. For $700 a night, I expected luxury, not excuses. Won't be back.

I really wanted to love the Monaco based on the photos, but our stay was a letdown from start to finish. Check-in took almost forty minutes because they were understaffed, and no one apologized. Our room faced the alley, so we heard garbage trucks at 5am both mornings despite requesting a quiet room weeks in advance. The air conditioning barely worked and the front desk just shrugged, offering nothing. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely. Breakfast was cold and the buffet ran out of most items by 9am. For the price, I expected far better service and basic comfort. Location is decent, but honestly that was the only redeeming thing. Won't be returning.

We stayed at the Omni for a long weekend and honestly expected much more for the price. Check-in took forever because they apparently had no record of our reservation, even though I had the confirmation email on my phone. The front desk staff weren't rude exactly, just completely indifferent. Our room smelled vaguely of smoke even though it was supposed to be non-smoking, and the air conditioner rattled all night like it was about to take off. The bed was okay, but the bathroom had visible grime in the corners and hair in the tub, which is just unacceptable. Room service took over an hour and arrived lukewarm. The location is convenient, I'll give it that, but with all the other hotels in the area, I won't be back. Truly disappointing for a place with this reputation.

I really wanted to like the Hotel Palmer, but our stay was a letdown from start to finish. Check-in took nearly forty minutes because the front desk was understaffed and the clerk seemed completely lost. Our room smelled faintly of mildew, the air conditioning rattled all night, and the 'city view' was basically a wall three feet from the window. The hairdryer didn't work, and housekeeping skipped our room entirely on the second day. Breakfast was the real low point--cold eggs, stale pastries, and the coffee machine broke down while we were standing there. Worse, nobody apologized or offered any kind of accommodation when we complained; we just got shrugs. For the price they charge, this place is seriously overrated. I won't be back, and I'd suggest looking elsewhere.

We stayed at the Sheraton for a long weekend and honestly expected better for the price. Check-in took almost forty minutes because the front desk seemed understaffed, and when we finally got to our room the air conditioning barely worked. We called twice about it and nobody came up until the next morning. The bed itself was fine, but the bathroom had hair in the tub and stale towels that I had to exchange myself at the housekeeping cart. Breakfast was the biggest letdown. Over $30 per person for cold eggs, watery oatmeal, and a coffee machine that kept jamming. The lobby looks impressive, sure, but the service behind it falls flat. Location is convenient, I'll give it that, yet with so many other hotels nearby, I won't be back here. Disappointing overall.

I really wanted to love this Sofitel given the price point, but the stay fell flat in almost every way. Check-in took nearly forty minutes because the front desk was understaffed, and no one apologized for the wait. My room had a strange musty smell, the AC rattled all night, and the 'luxury' bedding felt dated and slightly stained. Housekeeping skipped my room entirely one day and I had to call twice to get fresh towels. Breakfast was the biggest letdown--cold eggs, lukewarm coffee, and a buffet that looked picked over well before closing time. The concierge also gave me blatantly wrong directions twice. For a property charging these rates, the service and upkeep simply don't match. Honestly, I'd expected far more from a brand like this and won't be rushing back.

I really expected more from a property with the Swissotel name. Check-in took almost 40 minutes because the front desk seemed understaffed and confused about my reservation, and nobody apologized properly. The room itself was worn out: stained carpet, a shower head that dribbled water, and the AC made a rattling noise all night so I barely slept. Housekeeping skipped my room on the second day entirely and I had to call twice to get fresh towels. Breakfast was the biggest letdown; cold eggs, empty trays that stayed empty for 20 minutes, and a bill that somehow included items I never ordered. Location is convenient, sure, but at this price point I've stayed in much better hotels. For what they charge, the service should be flawless, not this sloppy. I won't be returning.

We stayed at the Talbott for a long weekend and honestly expected more for the price. The room was smaller than advertised and felt dated, with a wobbly AC unit that rattled all night. Housekeeping skipped our room entirely one day and we had to call twice to get fresh towels. The front desk staff were hit or miss--one person was friendly, another seemed annoyed by every question. Location is decent, but street noise came right through the thin windows. The 'complimentary coffee' in the lobby ran out by 9am both mornings. At these rates, I've had far better experiences elsewhere in the city. Probably won't be back.
